Tooth erosion is a health problem that is becoming increasingly common as a reflection of modern diet and lifestyle. Tooth enamel loss does not only cause aesthetic concerns, but can also lead to a number of health problems, including tooth sensitivity, cavities, and even tooth loss. Anyone can get tooth erosion. It is common in all age groups and affects approximately 50% of primary (baby) teeth and up to 45% of permanent (adult) teeth.

If this problem progresses, dental fillings or crowns may be needed. It is possible to stop the progression of erosion with early diagnosis and preventive measures. Therefore, it is important to go to the dentist regularly to prevent tooth erosion.
## Common Causes of Dental Erosion

Acidic foods and drinks are among the most common causes of tooth erosion. Especially acidic fruits such as lemons and grapefruits and fizzy drinks can damage tooth enamel due to their acid content. In addition, stomach acid can also cause acid erosion on teeth. So, although this condition may seem like two different health problems, acid reflux and tooth erosion are factors that affect each other. People with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) suffer from this condition. In addition, excessively harsh tooth brushing techniques and side effects of some medications can also contribute to tooth enamel erosion.
There are many different reasons that cause tooth erosion. The causes of tooth erosion are as follows:

Bruxism: This disease, also known as teeth grinding disorder, can lead to tooth erosion. When patients fall asleep at night, they unconsciously and involuntarily apply pressure to their teeth. When this happens every night, it causes tooth enamel to wear down and erosion over time.

Dry Mouth: The salivary glands help protect the teeth and gums in the mouth by producing adequate levels of saliva. If saliva production is inadequate, the mouth becomes dry and acids contribute to tooth sensitivity and erosion. Various medical conditions and side effects of medications can also cause dry mouth.

Diet Programs for weight loss: There is an important relationship between diet and tooth erosion. The foods we consume during the day, the snacks we have become accustomed to, and various foods can cause tooth erosion. Sweets cause tooth decay, bacteria formation, and this damages tooth enamel. In addition, when we do not eat enough or only consume fruits and vegetables while dieting, you can put both your general health and your oral and dental health at risk.

Various Problems in Digestion: One of the most important factors that cause tooth erosion is stomach acid. Because when it comes into the mouth and teeth, it negatively affects dental health. When stomach acid reaches the teeth due to digestive problems, it damages tooth enamel very much. In addition, when you wake up in the morning, discomforts such as nausea and vomiting also trigger stomach acid to reach the teeth and will lead to tooth erosion. Reflux will increase the stomach acid rate.
## Symptoms of Tooth Erosion

It is difficult to detect tooth erosion in the early stages of tooth erosion. Increasing tooth sensitivity is one of the most common early signs of tooth erosion. Changes in the appearance of teeth, such as teeth appearing more translucent or having rounded and smooth edges, may indicate that erosion is progressing.
Symptoms vary from person to person. Symptoms that indicate enamel erosion in the early stages are as follows:

As enamel erosion progresses, in other words, as it wears away more layers of your teeth, you may begin to feel pain. The effects of tooth erosion are likely to become more noticeable as the erosion gets closer to the tooth pulp.
The aim of treating tooth erosion is to repair existing damage and prevent its progression. Common treatment methods used are listed below:
## Protecting the Tooth and Reducing Sensitivity
For protecting enamel from erosion and strengthening it, fluoride gel or varnish can be applied. This also reduces sensitivity.
Special toothpastes or agents applied to the tooth surface to reduce sensitivity are one of the home remedies for tooth erosion.
### Fillings and Coatings
Dental fillings and coatings are the most commonly applied tooth erosion solutions.
In cases where enamel loss is severe, porcelain or zirconia coated tooth erosion repair is applied to protect the teeth and provide an aesthetic appearance.
### Gum Treatment
If erosion has caused gum recession or sensitivity, gum treatments may also be necessary.
### Diet and Lifestyle Changes
It is especially necessary to avoid carbonated drinks and foods. You should brush your teeth and drink water after meals. You should not consume starchy and sugary foods.
### Treatment of the Conditions that Cause Tooth Erosion

Reflux and dry mouth are two common causes of tooth erosion. These are also health problems. Therefore, these conditions need to be treated not only for tooth erosion treatment but also for general health.
Using mouth moisturizers or medications to increase saliva production in a dry mouth is one of the tooth erosion solutions to be applied at home.
## Professional Treatment for Tooth Erosion at Dentaliva

To maintain optimal oral health, you should visit your dentist regularly. Visiting your dentist at least once every six months is very important for oral and dental health. Tooth erosion is not an oral health problem that progresses quickly. You may feel this discomfort in the early stages of tooth erosion. In the early days of the problem, your dentist can give you dental advice for tooth erosion to stop its progression. Dentaliva offers you professional treatment for tooth erosion, as with other oral and dental treatments. If you experience sensitivity in your teeth or notice visual signs of tooth wear, such as chipping, pitting or discoloration, contact us without delay. Early treatment can prevent tooth erosion from getting worse.

Braces are an orthodontic treatment method used to correct problems such as misalignment of teeth, missing or extra teeth, and deviation of teeth from their normal positions. Orthodontic treatment cost varies depending on the degree of crookedness of the teeth, structural problems in the jaw and the materials used. Especially some situations such as teeth extracted in the past or wisdom teeth putting pressure on other teeth may be effective in the emergence of these problems.

Braces, one of the orthodontic treatment methods, are preferred to correct dental disorders. Braces prices may vary depending on various factors such as treatment duration, type of material, treatment method and the experience of the dentist. One of the factors that most affects the price scale is the level of deterioration in the tooth structure and the difficulty of treatment. Therefore, it is important to consult a qualified clinic to find out the average cost of braces and to have detailed information about the treatment process.
Factors Determining Braces Prices
Factors that are effective in determining the cost of braces are:
Treatment methods to be applied to one jaw or both jaws,
Type of material used for brackets and braces,
The rate of crooked teeth,
Position of the jaw (back or forward)
The amount of space between teeth,
Jaw stenosis or problems in palate structure,
Gums being more visible than normal.

Metal braces, porcelain braces and clear aligners are frequently preferred among the materials used during the treatment process. Single chin or double chin application is an important factor in changing prices. In general, metal braces prices are among the most affordable options, while porcelain and clear aligners are more costly. If there are very large gaps between the teeth and these gaps cannot be closed with existing teeth, implants can be applied after the treatment. However, implant costs are not included in braces treatment prices.
Types of Braces and Their Prices

Braces are a preferred orthodontic treatment method to fix crooked teeth and obtain an aesthetic smile. Pricing may vary depending on the type of material used, duration of treatment, specialty of the orthodontist and difficulty level of the treatment. Information about the most commonly used types of braces, their features and braces price comparison is provided below;
It is the most commonly used and affordable braces.
It is preferred for long-term treatments with its durable and solid structure.

It is more sensitive than metal braces and has a higher risk of breakage.

It is set on the back surface of the teeth, so it is completely invisible.
It is more ideal for people having aesthetic concerns.
Its application is more complex and its treatment period may be longer.
Hidden braces prices are the most expensive.
It is a system consisting of transparent plates instead of brace and brackets.
Since it is removable, it provides comfort while eating and brushing teeth.
It is suitable for mild tooth misalignments, but is not preferred in complex cases.
Since it is a high-tech product, its prices are high.
Clear Aligners vs Braces Price
Metal braces are budget-friendly and versatile, while clear aligners prioritize comfort and appearance. Treatment choice should balance cost, effectiveness, and personal preferences.
Is There an Age Limitation in Orthodontic Treatment?

Orthodontic treatments can be applied to people of all ages. However, treatment planning is shaped depending on the person’s age and needs. Porcelain braces are often preferred by adults because they address aesthetic concerns. In addition, orthodontic applications can be performed to prepare for prosthetic treatment.
Braces Treatment Process

Braces treatment is usually completed within 4 to 12 months. However, this period may vary between 1.5 and 2.5 years depending on the degree of distortion and treatment difficulties. Factors such as attending to sessions regularly, neglecting dental care, and breaking braces are effective in prolonging the treatment period. When the person makes a point of the treatment, the process ends successfully in a shorter time. Mild pain and small wounds on the cheeks may occur during the first sessions of treatment. However, this situation goes away by itself within a few days.
Braces Prices

How much do braces cost? Braces prices are calculated according to the minimum wage scale determined by the Turkish Dental Association (TDB) every year. Although treatment below this scale was prohibited in the past, this rule has become more flexible today. This situation leads to different pricing. The main reason why braces prices vary is that each treatment has a personalized and unique structure. What is the Hollywood Smile?

Hollywood smile refers to a series of procedures that have been popular for a long time and aim to give people a more aesthetic and pleasant smile. In this application, naturalness is prioritized and individuals are provided with a more attractive smile and perfect teeth. The definition of Hollywood smile comes from the fact that this procedure provides a similar appearance to the smiles of Hollywood stars.

This procedure, also known as smile aesthetics, provides harmony and aesthetic balance between lips, teeth and gums. Thus, it allows people to have a more elegant and impressive smile. Hollywood smiles for perfect teeth!

Hollywood smile treatment is not only preferred frequently by women but also by men. Smile aesthetics increases individuals’ self-confidence and helps them communicate with their environment more effectively.
What is a Hollywood Smile?

Hollywood smile is a method that is very popular in aesthetic dentistry and is known as a special smile design. Achieving the Hollywood smile inspired by the fascinating world of Hollywood includes a series of stages such as whitening the teeth, applying porcelain veneers if necessary, shaping the teeth and closing the gaps between the teeth.
Who Can Get a Hollywood Smile?

Anyone who is not satisfied with their teeth structure or wants to have a better tooth structure can have a Hollywood smile. The treatment process is customized to the person’s needs and differs for each individual. Therefore, there is no specific standard procedure. The important thing is to satisfy individuals’ expectations and their needs.

These procedures are generally performed painlessly and comfortably. Therefore, anesthesia is not needed. However, local anesthesia can be applied in some cases such as implanting application or removing large amounts of material from the tooth.
What are Hollywood Smile Procedures?

Hollywood smile design is customized to each individual’s needs and expectations. Therefore, the applied procedures may differ from person to person. However, the generally preferred and frequently applied procedures can be listed as follows:
Porcelain Veneer

Hollywood smile veneer is performed to give the smile an aesthetic appearance. In this procedure, a light abrasion is made on the surface of the teeth and then thin porcelain veneers are placed on the front parts of the teeth.

This method provides a more attractive smile by giving white, bright and smooth appearance to the teeth. It also helps to fill gaps between teeth, and to correct symmetry disorders. Porcelain veneer is one of the frequently preferred methods, especially in cases of excessive yellowing of teeth.
Teeth Whitening

White teeth play a big role in the striking beauty of the smiles of Hollywood stars. For this reason, Hollywood smile teeth whitening is frequently performed. However, this procedure may not be needed for every individual. If the individual’s tooth color already has the desired whiteness, this step can be skipped and other procedures can be carried out.
Implant Treatment

Having missing teeth is one of the factors that negatively affects the aesthetics of the smile. Implant treatment is one of the most effective methods to solve this problem. It has great importance for both a symmetrical tooth appearance and an aesthetic smile.
Hollywood Smile vs. Regular Veneers
The differences between Hollywood smile treatment and regular dental veneers become evident in terms of treatment purposes, materials used, design processes and aesthetic goals.

A Hollywood smile is an aesthetically focused and personalized treatment. If a perfect smile is desired rather than a natural appearance, this treatment is preferred. However, if you only want to veneer your teeth for functional or simple aesthetic reasons, regular veneers may be sufficient.

Hollywood Smile cost is higher than regular veneer costs since Hollywood smile requires more time, technology and aesthetic work. Regular Veneers are a more economical option and generally treatment-oriented.
Hollywood Smile Advantages

Hollywood smile design stands out with the many advantages it provides to people. One of the most obvious benefits of this procedure is that it increases individuals’ self-confidence. Some of the prominent advantages of the Hollywood smile design are an aesthetic and attractive smile, bright and white teeth, a symmetrical tooth structure, elimination of existing dental problems and healthy teeth and gums.
Hollywood Smile Before and After: The Power of Change
The Hollywood smile provides not only an aesthetic transformation but also self-confidence. Here is a brief summary of the change that occurred in this process:
Aesthetic Concerns: Hesitancy to smile due to crooked, gapped, yellowed or gum problems.
Limited Self-Confidence: Avoiding expressing oneself in social environments.
Functional Problems: Chewing difficulties or disorders in tooth alignment.
Perfect Smile: Symmetrical and smooth teeth with applications such as porcelain laminates, whitening and zirconium coatings.
Increased Self-Confidence: Communicating more easily in social and professional life.
Healthy Oral Structure: Strengthening the teeth functionally as well as aesthetically.
Hollywood Smile Dental Care: Secrets of a Shining Smile

A Hollywood smile means a healthy smile made up of pure white, perfect and aesthetic teeth. However, maintaining this appearance is possible with a correct dental care routine. Hollywood Smile Dental Care is briefly as follows: Regular Teeth Cleaning, Attention to Oral Hygiene, Teeth Whitening, Regular Dentist Check-ups, Nutrition and Habits (tea, coffee, cigarettes, etc.). These points are also the tips for long-lasting Hollywood smile care. The Hollywood smile is not only an aesthetic appearance but also a reflection of oral health. With the right care, anyone can have the smile of their dreams!
Hollywood Smile Prices

The Hollywood smile procedure, which is frequently preferred by those who want to have an aesthetic and perfect smile, also arouses curiosity with its price. As of 2024, choosing a clinic for Hollywood Smile varies depending on prices and individuals’ needs. That’s why, Hollywood smile cost also varies depending on each individual’s treatment plan. For example, only teeth whitening may be sufficient for some individuals, while others may require more extensive procedures such as implant treatment. Therefore, it is not possible to give a fixed price information for the Hollywood smile.
To get the most accurate price information, you can contact our clinic to create a personal treatment plan and get detailed information.

What is the Hollywood Smile?

Hollywood smile refers to a series of procedures that have been popular for a long time and aim to give people a more aesthetic and pleasant smile. In this application, naturalness is prioritized and individuals are provided with a more attractive smile and perfect teeth. The definition of Hollywood smile comes from the fact that this procedure provides a similar appearance to the smiles of Hollywood stars.

This procedure, also known as smile aesthetics, provides harmony and aesthetic balance between lips, teeth and gums. Thus, it allows people to have a more elegant and impressive smile. Hollywood smiles for perfect teeth!

Hollywood smile treatment is not only preferred frequently by women but also by men. Smile aesthetics increases individuals’ self-confidence and helps them communicate with their environment more effectively.
## What is a Hollywood Smile?

Hollywood smile is a method that is very popular in aesthetic dentistry and is known as a special smile design. Achieving the Hollywood smile inspired by the fascinating world of Hollywood includes a series of stages such as whitening the teeth, applying porcelain veneers if necessary, shaping the teeth and closing the gaps between the teeth.
## Who Can Get a Hollywood Smile?

Anyone who is not satisfied with their teeth structure or wants to have a better tooth structure can have a Hollywood smile. The treatment process is customized to the person’s needs and differs for each individual. Therefore, there is no specific standard procedure. The important thing is to satisfy individuals’ expectations and their needs.

These procedures are generally performed painlessly and comfortably. Therefore, anesthesia is not needed. However, local anesthesia can be applied in some cases such as implanting application or removing large amounts of material from the tooth.
## What are Hollywood Smile Procedures?

Hollywood smile design is customized to each individual’s needs and expectations. Therefore, the applied procedures may differ from person to person. However, the generally preferred and frequently applied procedures can be listed as follows:
### Porcelain Veneer

Hollywood smile veneer is performed to give the smile an aesthetic appearance. In this procedure, a light abrasion is made on the surface of the teeth and then thin porcelain veneers are placed on the front parts of the teeth.

This method provides a more attractive smile by giving white, bright and smooth appearance to the teeth. It also helps to fill gaps between teeth, and to correct symmetry disorders. Porcelain veneer is one of the frequently preferred methods, especially in cases of excessive yellowing of teeth.
### Teeth Whitening

White teeth play a big role in the striking beauty of the smiles of Hollywood stars. For this reason, Hollywood smile teeth whitening is frequently performed. However, this procedure may not be needed for every individual. If the individual’s tooth color already has the desired whiteness, this step can be skipped and other procedures can be carried out.
### Implant Treatment

Having missing teeth is one of the factors that negatively affects the aesthetics of the smile. Implant treatment is one of the most effective methods to solve this problem. It has great importance for both a symmetrical tooth appearance and an aesthetic smile.
## Hollywood Smile vs. Regular Veneers
The differences between Hollywood smile treatment and regular dental veneers become evident in terms of treatment purposes, materials used, design processes and aesthetic goals.

A Hollywood smile is an aesthetically focused and personalized treatment. If a perfect smile is desired rather than a natural appearance, this treatment is preferred. However, if you only want to veneer your teeth for functional or simple aesthetic reasons, regular veneers may be sufficient.

Hollywood Smile cost is higher than regular veneer costs since Hollywood smile requires more time, technology and aesthetic work. Regular Veneers are a more economical option and generally treatment-oriented.
## Hollywood Smile Advantages

Hollywood smile design stands out with the many advantages it provides to people. One of the most obvious benefits of this procedure is that it increases individuals’ self-confidence. Some of the prominent advantages of the Hollywood smile design are an aesthetic and attractive smile, bright and white teeth, a symmetrical tooth structure, elimination of existing dental problems and healthy teeth and gums.
## Hollywood Smile Before and After: The Power of Change
The Hollywood smile provides not only an aesthetic transformation but also self-confidence. Here is a brief summary of the change that occurred in this process:
Aesthetic Concerns: Hesitancy to smile due to crooked, gapped, yellowed or gum problems.
Limited Self-Confidence: Avoiding expressing oneself in social environments.
Functional Problems: Chewing difficulties or disorders in tooth alignment.
Perfect Smile: Symmetrical and smooth teeth with applications such as porcelain laminates, whitening and zirconium coatings.
Increased Self-Confidence: Communicating more easily in social and professional life.
Healthy Oral Structure: Strengthening the teeth functionally as well as aesthetically.
## Hollywood Smile Dental Care: Secrets of a Shining Smile

A Hollywood smile means a healthy smile made up of pure white, perfect and aesthetic teeth. However, maintaining this appearance is possible with a correct dental care routine. Hollywood Smile Dental Care is briefly as follows: Regular Teeth Cleaning, Attention to Oral Hygiene, Teeth Whitening, Regular Dentist Check-ups, Nutrition and Habits (tea, coffee, cigarettes, etc.). These points are also the tips for long-lasting Hollywood smile care. The Hollywood smile is not only an aesthetic appearance but also a reflection of oral health. With the right care, anyone can have the smile of their dreams!
## Hollywood Smile Prices

The Hollywood smile procedure, which is frequently preferred by those who want to have an aesthetic and perfect smile, also arouses curiosity with its price. As of 2024, choosing a clinic for Hollywood Smile varies depending on prices and individuals’ needs. That’s why, Hollywood smile cost also varies depending on each individual’s treatment plan. For example, only teeth whitening may be sufficient for some individuals, while others may require more extensive procedures such as implant treatment. Therefore, it is not possible to give a fixed price information for the Hollywood smile.
To get the most accurate price information, you can contact our clinic to create a personal treatment plan and get detailed information.

Total dentures, also known as full dentures, are removable dentures that are placed on the upper and lower jaws with tissue support in cases where all teeth in the mouth are lost due to various reasons such as decay, osteoporosis and trauma. This treatment is applied to people who have lost their chewing function due to the lack of natural teeth. It is an undeniable fact that good chewing is very important in the digestion of nutrients. In addition to regaining the ability to chew, total dentures are also very effective in regaining an aesthetic appearance. Due to these total dental denture benefits, this treatment is one of the most important treatments among oral and dental treatments.

Total denture can be designed to replace all teeth in the mouth, or it can be designed to replace only the upper teeth or lower teeth. Complete upper denture is applied to replace all upper teeth. It is a method applied to people with healthy lower teeth, without giving up their own teeth, to replace only the upper teeth. When upper and lower dentures are attached together, it is called a full set of dentures.
Full Mouth Prosthesis Stages

Total prosthesis treatment begins with the denture consultation and planning stage. At this point, the dentist evaluates the patient’s general health status in detail and examines the oral structure. Then, he/she receives brief information about the tooth deficiency. This evaluation is the first step taken to find the most suitable tooth replacement solutions and create a plan.

Measurement and Modeling: Measurement is very important for the prosthesis to fit in the most accurate and comfortable way. Although denture adjustments are made later, the patient’s first experiences with denture materials should be problem-free. The dentist takes the measurements that are most suitable for the patient’s oral structure in detail and these measurements are sent to the laboratory. Based on these measurements, laboratories create special custom dentures for the patient. In the modeling process, the functional and aesthetic needs of the prosthesis are definitely taken into consideration.

Prosthesis Making and Adjustment: The prosthesis produced in the laboratory must definitely go through special applications to adapt to the patient’s oral structure. The form, color and aesthetic features of the prosthesis are carefully determined to be compatible with the patient’s natural teeth. As a result of the examination and rehearsals, the aim is to use the prosthesis and provide a natural appearance.

Rehearsals and Final Check-up: After the prosthesis is ready, the final trial is performed and the prosthesis is checked to see if it fits. At this point, the important thing is to meet the patient’s aesthetic expectations and ensure that they have a comfortable use.
Total Denture Care
In order to use your dentures for many years without any problems, you need to perform regular maintenance. The main points to consider in total denture maintenance are as follows:
Keeping the dentures dry can lead to structural deformations. Store your dentures in a container full of water or in denture liquid when not in use.
Dentures are vulnerable to impacts. Filling the sink with water or laying down a soft towel during cleaning reduces the risk of damage when dropped.
Your dentist should check them at least once a year. The dentist evaluates the fit of the denture and makes the necessary adjustments.

Avoid cleaning dentures with bleach or strong chemicals. These substances can weaken the structure of the denture. One of the most common denture maintenance mistakes is using chemicals that damage the full set of dentures.
Total Denture Cleaning

Cleaning of total dentures is necessary to both protect oral health and increase the durability of dentures. If food residues and plaque accumulated on the dentures are not cleaned, they can cause bad odor, infection and gum disease.
After meals, remove the dentures and rinse them under warm water. This process removes food residues and bacteria accumulated on the surface.
Brush your dentures with a soft brush and special cleaning pastes made for dentures. Ordinary toothpastes can damage the surface of the denture.
Avoid applying excessive pressure to the dentures while brushing, as this can cause scratches on the surface.
At the end of the day, you can leave your dentures in denture cleaning boxes containing warm water. These boxes help clean stains and bacteria formed on the surface of the dentures.
Use of Total Dentures

It is common to feel like the new denture is a large and foreign object in the mouth when using a total denture. At first, a swelling is felt in the cheeks and lips. No matter how thin the dentures are, they feel swollen to the user during the adaptation process. Since the lower denture moves more, it is more likely to come out of place. Getting used to a lower denture is much more difficult than getting used to an upper denture and it takes time. In the first days, there may be an increase in the amount of saliva due to the stimulation of the secretory glands. This passes over time. No matter how much care is taken in the construction of the dentures as they fit into the soft tissue and move during use, they can cause discomfort in some places. Adjustments and denture repairs should be applied to the dentures at the right time.

In any negative situation, the patient trying to solve the problem himself can cause bigger problems. As long as the tissues in the mouth adapt to the denture within a few weeks, some problems can disappear without intervention. It is very rare for there to be no complaints after the denture installation process is completed.

Total dentures are a treatment that is completed in approximately 5 sessions. Since there will be day gaps between sessions, the average duration is 15 days. However, this period may vary when considering the tooth tissue and various physical sensitivities of the patient. Total dentures offer a treatment solution that meets expectations by completing all the teeth of individuals who have no teeth left. These dentures are made of acrylate materials. They are placed on the gums, that is, on the lower and upper jaw bones. In this way, they both replace the lost teeth.

The prices of total dentures may vary depending on the technology, material, laboratory and experience of the dentist. In this sense, complete dentures can be considered a very important treatment option for patients who have lost their natural teeth. It is necessary to get detailed information about dentures. It is possible to have aesthetic teeth by making the right choice. Taking care of the dentures and taking into account the dentist’s recommendations extends the life of the dentures and protects oral health.

Oral Health and Dental Care for the Elderly

Protecting dental health in old age is very important not only for oral and dental health but also for general health and quality of life. As people get older, dental care becomes more difficult. As a result, teeth become more sensitive to external factors and their protection becomes more difficult. For this reason, dental hygiene for older adults is very important.

The reason why oral health for the elderly deteriorates is not only aging. This very common idea is not completely true. Oral health in people can deteriorate at any age for many reasons. Some factors that deteriorate this oral health are as follows:
Not performing oral care regularly every day as it should be,
Not visiting dentists regularly and having check-ups,

Oral care with these factors causes deterioration of the tooth structure not only in the elderly but in everyone. However, it is also a fact that older people who pay attention to their oral care have a much better dental structure than young people who do not pay attention to oral care.
Maintaining Oral Health in Old Age

Maintaining oral health in old age is one of the most important factors affecting the general health of the elderly. Gum disease, tooth loss, dry mouth and chewing difficulties are common dental issues in seniors. These problems can be seen more frequently than in younger ages. It is extremely important to maintain regular tooth brushing and flossing habits to protect oral health. In addition, individuals using dental implants for older adults should not neglect denture care. Dental visits for the elderly are very important for dental care for seniors.
A balanced diet provides calcium and vitamin D, which support tooth and gum health. In addition, not smoking and drinking alcohol is preventive dental care for the elderly.

Regular dentist check-ups allow for early diagnosis of problems that may arise due to age. Conditions such as dry mouth in particular are a common problem encountered during the aging process and can be controlled with salivary gland stimulating treatments or special oral care products. Dentists can also offer individualized recommendations to prevent gum recession, cavities, and other problems. Elderly oral hygiene both improves quality of life and helps prevent general health problems.
Common Dental Issues in Seniors

As people age, their dental health usually requires more attention and care. Tooth loss is one of the most common problems encountered in the elderly. Therefore, tooth loss prevention for the elderly is quite important. Oral hygiene practices for older adults is one of the most important practices for a healthy mouth and teeth in the elderly.

Tooth loss is another common dental issue in seniors. The most commonly preferred method for treating tooth loss in the elderly is dentures. However, improper fit of dentures or their loss of fit over time can lead to discomfort such as chewing difficulties and mouth sores. In addition, tooth enamel erosion and sensitivity in the teeth are also common problems experienced by the elderly. This can cause discomfort when eating or drinking something hot, cold or sweet.
Another important problem is dry mouth. The decrease in saliva production with age or the side effects of the medications used can lead to dry mouth.

Dry mouth treatment for the elderly involves both addressing the underlying causes and alleviating the symptoms. Individuals with dry mouth should drink water regularly. They should not consume products that can increase dryness, such as caffeine and alcohol. They can use sugar-free gum or lozenges containing xylitol to help increase saliva production. For temporary relief, saliva-replacing mouth sprays or moisturizing gels can be preferred. If dry mouth is caused by medications, alternative medications or dosage adjustments can be made by consulting a doctor or dentist. In addition, taking care of oral hygiene and using toothpastes containing fluoride helps prevent cavities and gum problems that dry mouth can cause. Dental care routines for seniors are important for effective management of this condition.

Problems such as gingivitis and periodontitis can have serious consequences, including tooth loss, if left untreated. In addition, the incidence of oral cancer increases with age. Therefore, regular dentist check-ups and oral health awareness for seniors are of great importance not only for dental health but also for general health. A balanced diet, a good oral hygiene routine and regular professional care are essential for maintaining dental health in older individuals.

If you are suffering from receding gums, you should know that the exposed root surfaces are softer than tooth enamel and can decay more quickly. In this case, tooth decay can quickly reach the nerves of your teeth and cause inflammation, or the tooth can completely break from the root. You may have had fillings in your mouth until now, and it may be time to replace these fillings. Tooth decay progresses under broken, cracked or leaking fillings. For this reason, it is very important to continue to visit the dentist regularly, even if you do not feel pain.
Dental Care Tips for Elderly
Teeth Cleaning for Seniors: The first of the dental care tips for the elderly is regular brushing of the teeth. Brush your teeth at least twice a day with fluoride toothpaste and floss.
Denture care for the elderly: If you have dentures, clean them daily and remove them before going to bed at night so that they can rest comfortably.
Dry Mouth Treatment for the Elderly: Drink water frequently and regularly. Increase and maintain saliva production by using sugar-free gum or lozenges.
Healthy Diet: Avoid sugary and acidic foods, eat vegetables, fruits and foods containing calcium to support dental health.
Regular Dentist Check Ups: Visit your dentist at least twice a year; have your dentures checked for fit, cavities and other oral health problems.
Choosing the Right Brush and Technique: Brush your teeth gently using a soft-bristled toothbrush and avoid brushing too hard.

Oral Health and Dental Care for the Elderly

Protecting dental health in old age is very important not only for oral and dental health but also for general health and quality of life. As people get older, dental care becomes more difficult. As a result, teeth become more sensitive to external factors and their protection becomes more difficult. For this reason, dental hygiene for older adults is very important.

The reason why oral health for the elderly deteriorates is not only aging. This very common idea is not completely true. Oral health in people can deteriorate at any age for many reasons. Some factors that deteriorate this oral health are as follows:
Not performing oral care regularly every day as it should be,
Not visiting dentists regularly and having check-ups,

Oral care with these factors causes deterioration of the tooth structure not only in the elderly but in everyone. However, it is also a fact that older people who pay attention to their oral care have a much better dental structure than young people who do not pay attention to oral care.
## Maintaining Oral Health in Old Age

Maintaining oral health in old age is one of the most important factors affecting the general health of the elderly. Gum disease, tooth loss, dry mouth and chewing difficulties are common dental issues in seniors. These problems can be seen more frequently than in younger ages. It is extremely important to maintain regular tooth brushing and flossing habits to protect oral health. In addition, individuals using dental implants for older adults should not neglect denture care. Dental visits for the elderly are very important for dental care for seniors.
A balanced diet provides calcium and vitamin D, which support tooth and gum health. In addition, not smoking and drinking alcohol is preventive dental care for the elderly.

Regular dentist check-ups allow for early diagnosis of problems that may arise due to age. Conditions such as dry mouth in particular are a common problem encountered during the aging process and can be controlled with salivary gland stimulating treatments or special oral care products. Dentists can also offer individualized recommendations to prevent gum recession, cavities, and other problems. Elderly oral hygiene both improves quality of life and helps prevent general health problems.
## Common Dental Issues in Seniors

As people age, their dental health usually requires more attention and care. Tooth loss is one of the most common problems encountered in the elderly. Therefore, tooth loss prevention for the elderly is quite important. Oral hygiene practices for older adults is one of the most important practices for a healthy mouth and teeth in the elderly.

Tooth loss is another common dental issue in seniors. The most commonly preferred method for treating tooth loss in the elderly is dentures. However, improper fit of dentures or their loss of fit over time can lead to discomfort such as chewing difficulties and mouth sores. In addition, tooth enamel erosion and sensitivity in the teeth are also common problems experienced by the elderly. This can cause discomfort when eating or drinking something hot, cold or sweet.
Another important problem is dry mouth. The decrease in saliva production with age or the side effects of the medications used can lead to dry mouth.

Dry mouth treatment for the elderly involves both addressing the underlying causes and alleviating the symptoms. Individuals with dry mouth should drink water regularly. They should not consume products that can increase dryness, such as caffeine and alcohol. They can use sugar-free gum or lozenges containing xylitol to help increase saliva production. For temporary relief, saliva-replacing mouth sprays or moisturizing gels can be preferred. If dry mouth is caused by medications, alternative medications or dosage adjustments can be made by consulting a doctor or dentist. Transparent Plaque Treatment and Prices

Transparent plaque is an orthodontic treatment which is an alternative to braces for suitable patients. This treatment is applied to pull the teeth to where they should be in cases where the teeth are not positioned properly, crooked and irregularly aligned. This treatment is also applied to straighten teeth.
There are some reasons why transparent plaque treatment is preferred. It does not cause an unpleasant appearance in the mouth. It can be removed and put back by the patient before eating.

This treatment is usually applied to treat slightly or moderately crooked teeth or small tooth gaps. Patients with excessive crookedness and gap problems in their teeth or patients with crossbite problems are treated with more complicated methods and devices.

Transparent plaques used in transparent plaque treatment are produced specifically depending on treatment plans using transparent and flexible plastic or acrylic material.They align the teeth by fitting tightly. They are also effective in strengthening teeth. They can be easily removed for eating and brushing and can be placed on the teeth by the patient.
How is Clear Plaque Treatment Performed?

After examining your teeth, the dentist or orthodontist takes a 3-D image of your mouth and jaw. Your dentist or orthodontist creates a plan to move your work in the right direction according to this image.
Then, a transparent plaque that will provide the new order is produced for the patient. The dentist attaches this plate to the patient’s teeth and teaches the patient how to wear it.
The transparent plaque attached to the teeth pushes the teeth in the direction they should be. The patient should wear the transparent plaque for approximately 20-22 hours every day.
After 1-2 weeks, the teeth complete the first stage of progression and the dentist creates a new plaque design after examining the patient.
The dental plate treatment process is completed with regular check-ups and the use of new transparent plaques until the patient’s teeth reach the state the dentist wants them to reach.

The duration of the clear plate treatment varies from person to person. The treatment usually lasts between 10 and 24 months. If the problem in the teeth has not progressed, the treatment can be completed in 6 months.

Some age groups are more advantageous in transparent plaque treatment. According to a study conducted on 30 volunteers, the speed of teeth moving in the mouth is faster between the ages of 35-50 compared to other age groups. Due to this factor, it is thought that transparent plaque is more effective in this age group. In the same study, it was determined that the movement of the teeth of women between the ages of 50-70 did not decrease as much as that of men.
Transparent Plaque Treatment Pricing
Transparent plaque treatment requires the use of more than one plate. This may increase the cost.
The irregularity in the alignment of the teeth affects the number of transparent plates to be used. Therefore, the treatment pricing varies from patient to patient.

On the other hand, the technology and materials used in the production of transparent dental plaques are also an important factor in the treatment price. Plaques produced with more advanced technology and high quality materials are more expensive.
Advantages of Transparent Plaque Treatment
The advantages of using dental plates, which are often made of flexible plastic material, are as follows:
Unobtrusive Appearance: This treatment method does not draw attention in the mouth and does not cause an uncomfortable appearance because no wires or brackets are used.
A Fast Healing Process: Transparent dental plates can create a proper tooth alignment after six months of use.

Removable: Transparent plaque can be removed at any time. Therefore, it allows for easy dental care. In this way, you can remove the dental plaque before eating, brush your teeth after eating and re-wear your transparent plate.
More Comfortable Than Braces: Compared to braces, transparent plaque is more flexible and therefore allows for easier and more comfortable treatment.
How to Remove Transparent Plaques
You can follow these steps to remove transparent plaques used in dental treatment from your mouth:
Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water before removing transparent plaques. This is important for the plaques and your oral hygiene.

Start removing your transparent plaques with one of the upper or lower plates. Do not try to remove the plates from both jaws at the same time. Remove them with your fingers. Using any device can damage the plaques.
Hold your plate by lifting its edges and carefully pull it in the direction of the removal. Do this process slowly and carefully until you have completely removed them from your teeth.
After removing one side of the plate, remove the other side in the same way. Do not try to do this process for the upper and lower plaques at the same time.
Brush your teeth and clean the plates after completely removing the plaques. Keep your plates in their special case to prevent damage and to keep them hygienic.
Take a Step to a Perfect Smile with Dentaliva
Examination and Planning: Our expert dentists analyze your tooth structure and determine whether transparent plaques are suitable for you.
Digital Simulation: Advanced technologies provide the opportunity to see the post-treatment appearance of your teeth on the screen in advance.

Plaque Production and Use: Custom-made plaques are delivered to you with a special user guide. You can achieve proper tooth alignment by wearing the plaque regularly throughout the process recommended by your dentist. New plaques can be produced for you according to the healing status of your teeth during the treatment period.
Periodic Checks: During the treatment, tooth movements are monitored with periodic checks and necessary adjustments are made.

Dentaliva offers you a reliable, modern and effective solution to reach the smile of your dreams with transparent dental plate treatment. If you want to get rid of small or large irregularities in your teeth and do this almost invisibly, we will be happy to see you at Dentaliva.

A cracked or broken tooth is one of the most common dental problems that can cause bigger problems. Due to the potential of broken and cracked teeth, they need to be examined and treated as soon as possible. When a tooth is broken, a person feels no pain or very little pain because tooth enamel has no nerves or blood vessels. The fact that a broken tooth does not cause pain does not mean that it does not need treatment. Because the biggest purpose of applying broken tooth treatment in the first stage is to prevent bigger problems in the future.
If a broken or cracked tooth is not treated early on, some discomforts that will be experienced are as follows:
Sensitivity to hot or cold
Discomfort in the palate, lips and mouth,

Teeth can break for different reasons. Before applying the appropriate dental practice among dental treatments, it is important to determine how the tooth broke. Because the most appropriate treatment type is preferred depending on the way the tooth broke.
A crack in a tooth can sometimes cause the tooth to split in two. This is usually experienced in cases of cracked teeth from the tooth surface to the gum line.
In another case, a vertical crack forms on the tooth surface up to the gum line.
Some tooth cracks start below the gum line and progress upwards.
There may be many small and thin cracks in the tooth enamel. The fact that they do not cause any discomfort in the mouth does not mean that the tooth will not weaken.
Why Do Teeth Break?

There are many different reasons why teeth can break. Moreover, there are different situations that increase the risk of tooth breakage. The most common reason for tooth breakage is exposure to impact. Biting a very hard object, having an accident or falling, doing hard sports without protecting the mouth area are all impacts that teeth can be exposed to. In addition to these, grinding your teeth while sleeping is another reason that most often leads to tooth breakage.

Other factors that increase the risk of tooth fractures include tooth decay, weakened tooth enamel, large and wide fillings, constant consumption of highly acidic foods and drinks, excessive sugar production and age-related erosion of tooth enamel, eating disorders, and excessive alcohol consumption.
Broken Tooth Treatment Ways
Broken or cracked teeth are treated individually. In other words, it is definitely not right to apply the same treatment to every patient.

If you have a broken tooth, it is essential to see a dentist without wasting time to protect your teeth and oral health. However, it is also possible to take various precautions before being examined. You should apply a cold compress to prevent possible swelling, rinse your mouth with salt water and clean your teeth, and use nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs to reduce pain and prevent swelling. Later, during the dentist’s examination, various treatment methods can be decided according to the condition of the broken or cracked tooth.
Commonly preferred treatment methods for broken teeth are as follows:

Porcelain Lamina: Porcelain Laminate: Porcelain laminate treatment, which is among the most popular aesthetic dentistry applications within the scope of smile aesthetics, is one of the most effective treatment methods for the front broken or cracked teeth. Leaf porcelains restore the natural appearance of broken and cracked teeth.
Bonding: This method is to add special composite materials to the teeth. It is another preferred method in broken tooth treatments. The dentist decides whether the procedure will be applied or not.
Filling: One of the most reliable and common treatment methods for treating broken teeth is filling. It is a treatment method that involves filling the cracks in a small part of the teeth.

Toothache During Pregnancy and Its Treatment
Toothache during pregnancy is an important issue for the health of both the expectant mother and the baby. During pregnancy, hormonal changes can affect tooth and gum health.
Causes of Toothache During Pregnancy
Hormonal Changes
Increased progesterone and estrogen hormones during pregnancy can increase blood flow to the gums, leading to swelling and tenderness. This can cause dental problems and inflammation of the gums..
Gum Diseases
Gum diseases may develop or existing diseases may get worse during pregnancy. Periodontitis is a serious gum disease that can cause tooth loss and may increase the risk of premature birth.
Calcium Deficiency

The body’s need for calcium increases during pregnancy. When calcium isn’t taken enough, the body withdraws the calcium it needs from bones and teeth, which can cause teeth to weaken and cause pain. Therefore, pregnant women should pay attention to their oral and dental health and be more scheduled in their dental appointments against the risk of tooth decay.
Nutritional Habits: Increased carbohydrate consumption during pregnancy can accelerate the formation of tooth decay. Foods and drinks with acidic affect stomach acid and can also damage tooth enamel.
Effects of Toothache on Pregnancy

Toothache can make pregnancy difficult. Constant pain can disrupt sleep patterns, cause morning sickness, increase stress levels, and reduce overall quality of life. Additionally, poor oral health can negatively affect the baby’s development. It has also been shown that there is a relationship between gum disease and premature birth and low birth weight.
Ways to Cope with Toothache During Pregnancy
Regular Dentist Check-ups

Visiting your dentist regularly during pregnancy helps you detect possible problems in advance. Teeth cleaning and control is one of the most effective ways to prevent gum diseases. When we perform dental procedures regularly, we can prevent gum bleeding, bacterial infections and increased bacterial tooth plaque.
Pay Attention to Dental Care
Brush your teeth with fluoride toothpaste at least twice a day and use dental floss. Mouthwashes can be effective in maintaining gum health.
Healthy Nutrition

Consuming foods rich in calcium is important for the health of both you and your baby. It also helps you maintain hormonal balance and hormone levels. It is very important to include calcium sources such as milk, cheese and yoghurt in your diet.
Painkillers

If toothache bothers you so much, you can use a safe painkiller as recommended by your doctor. Some medications, such as aspirin, should be avoided during pregnancy, so you should not use medication without consulting your doctor.
Natural Methods
Washing with warm salt water can relieve inflammation in the gums. Natural painkillers such as clove oil can also be used, but these must also have a doctor’s approval.

Periodontitis causes pockets to form below the gum line, which allows bacteria to accumulate. These pockets become a constant source of infection in the gums and continue to negatively affect gum health.

Aesthetic dentistry is a branch of dentistry that aims to improve the aesthetic appearance of teeth, gums and smile. These dental practices aim to help patients have a more beautiful and confident smile. Aesthetic dentistry uses a variety of methods and technologies to ensure that teeth are not only healthy but also look aesthetically pleasing. In other words, aesthetic dentistry meets both cosmetic and functional needs. In other words, aesthetic dentistry meets both cosmetic and functional needs.

Aesthetic dentistry aims to design the most aesthetic and harmonious smile for the individual by arranging different physical areas such as the shape of the individual’s teeth, the brightness and tone of the teeth, the size of the teeth, the appearance of the gums, the posture and fullness of the lips, and gum health. For this reason, aesthetic dentistry practices are often referred to as smile design.
Why is Aesthetic Dentistry Needed Most?

Poor oral and dental care, dental and gum diseases, tooth loss, tooth discoloration, fractures or cracks can cause the appearance of the teeth to become uncomfortable for people, especially when smiling. Even if there is no serious dental aesthetic problem, sometimes people want to have a better and more impressive smile and bright and beautiful teeth.
Methods Used in Aesthetic Dentistry

Denteliva’s specialist dentists determine the aesthetic dentistry methods to be used individually and plan the treatment, taking into account the person’s oral and dental structure and expectations from dental aesthetics. The methods used in aesthetic dentistry can be used alone or different methods can be used together depending on the designed tooth structure. The most commonly applied methods in aesthetic dentistry are as follows:

Teeth Whitening: It is a method used to give teeth a brighter and whiter appearance. Generally, there are two types of teeth whitening methods. One is the method that dentists apply in clinics, and the other is the method that people apply themselves at home. This process removes stains and discolorations on teeth.
Laminate Veneer: It is the process of bonding thin porcelain layers to the front surface of the teeth. It is used to correct the aesthetic appearance of cracked, broken, discolored or deformed teeth.
Bonding: It is the process of shaping a tooth-colored composite resin by applying it to the tooth surface. Small chips are used to close cracks or gaps between teeth.

Inlay and Onlay Restorations: These are porcelain or composite resin restorations used to treat major tooth decay or fillings. This method provides an aesthetic and functional solution by preserving the natural structure of the teeth.

Braces and Clear Aligners: These are orthodontic treatments used to ensure the alignment and proper alignment of the teeth. Transparent aligners have a more aesthetic appearance than traditional metal braces.

Dental Implants: It is the process of placing titanium screws with the function of natural tooth roots into the jawbone to replace missing teeth. Missing teeth are completed aesthetically and functionally by placing an artificial tooth on the titanium screws.

Gingivoplasty: These are surgical procedures performed to correct the gum line and obtain a symmetrical appearance. It can be applied by cutting the gums in cases where they are excessive or by adding them in cases where they are missing.

Aesthetic Tooth Filling: Aesthetic dental filling is a filling made on the teeth using composite material and filling material in natural tooth color. Thanks to the aesthetic filling, the filling part of the tooth is not noticed as a filling in the tooth because it is the same or very similar to the color and texture of the natural tooth.

Zirconium Dental Coating: Zirconium is a dental coating consisting of a metal-free and white material. It is used to cover the tooth surfaces of individuals who want to have aesthetic, beautiful and bright white teeth.
Benefits of Aesthetic Dentistry Applications
Aesthetically pleasing teeth increase the individual’s self-confidence and enable him to smile more comfortably in social life.
Aesthetic dental treatments often improve dental health as well. For example, properly aligned teeth are easier to clean. This reduces the risk of gum diseases.
Modern aesthetic dentistry techniques provide results that closely resemble natural teeth. This allows patients to have a natural and attractive smile.
Aesthetic treatments also improve the function of teeth. For example, properly aligned teeth offer better chewing and speaking functions.
Contact Detaliva for Aesthetic Dentistry

Dentaliva Dental Clinic aims to provide the best service to its patients with its expert staff and state-of-the-art equipment in aesthetic dental treatment. With personalized treatment plans, we ensure that everyone has a natural and beautiful smile. Our friendly and professional team offers you a comfortable and safe experience during the treatment process.
Contact Dentaliva Dental Clinic to get more information about aesthetic dental treatment and benefit from our special solutions. Let’s beautify your smile together!

Sinus lift surgery is a surgical procedure performed on patients who do not have sufficient bone height before dental implant treatment. This surgery aims to provide sufficient bone support for implants to be placed on the teeth in the back area of ​​the upper jaw. As a result of the expansion of the sinus cavity, the appropriate amount of bone to place an implant may not be available, especially in cases where the upper jaw bone structure is inadequate. Sinus lifting surgery is a safe and effective method to solve this problem.
Stages of Sinus Lifting Surgery
The condition of the sinuses and jawbone is examined before surgery using imaging methods such as x-ray and tomography. This evaluation provides the information needed to make the surgery successful.
The surgery is usually performed with local anesthesia. In some cases, sedation may be applied to ensure the comfort of the patient.
The surgeon lifts the sinus membrane by opening a small window in the upper jaw bone. This space created under the sinus membrane is made ready for bone grafting.

Bone graft material is placed under the sinus membrane. This material can be taken from the patient’s own bone tissue, or synthetic or animal-derived bone grafts can also be used. This graft fuses with the patient’s own bone tissue over time and creates sufficient bone volume.
Once the bone graft is placed, the area is closed and the healing process begins. Time to heal usually takes several months. During this time, the bone graft fuses with the natural bone tissue.
Can Sinus Lifting Surgery be Performed on Anyone?

This process can be applied to anyone. But in some cases there may be exceptions. These conditions may prevent sinus lifting surgery. This procedure performed for the implant helps the unsuitable dental bones gain volume and become suitable.

The bone structure of the person must be suitable for the sinus lifting surgical procedure. People need to complete tooth and bone growth. Since the incomplete bone structure may complete itself in the future, it is not desired to damage the structure.

This surgical procedure is performed on people over the age of twenty, as well as on people who have completed their tooth and bone development. For this procedure, if the patient has any allergic or chronic disease, the patient must inform the dentist and surgeon in advance.
Types of Sinus Removal Surgery

Sinus lift surgery aims to create sufficient bone volume in the back areas of the upper jaw for dental implant placement. There are different techniques for this surgery, and the method to be chosen depends on the patient’s needs and the condition of the jawbone.
Lateral Sinus Lift Surgery

Lateral Sinus Lift Surgery is the preferred method for patients with severe bone loss in the upper jaw. In this technique, a lateral window is opened into the sinus cavity to access the sinus membrane, the membrane is carefully lifted and a bone graft is placed.
Stages of Lateral Sinus Lift Surgery
An incision is made in the gum on the side of the upper jaw and the bone surface is seen.
A small window is opened and the sinus membrane is carefully lifted.
Bone graft material is placed under the sinus membrane.
The window and gum are closed and fixed with stitches.
Advantages of Lateral Sinus Lift Surgery
It provides the opportunity to create larger bone volume. This is a suitable method for patients with advanced bone loss.
Internal Sinus Lift Surgery

Internal Sinus Lift Surgery is a less invasive method and is generally suitable for patients with mild bone loss. In this technique, the sinus membrane is accessed directly from the implant socket during dental implant placement.
Stages of Internal Sinus Lift Surgery
The gum in the area where the implant will be placed is cut slightly.
While creating the implant slot, the sinus membrane is carefully reached.
The sinus membrane is gently lifted and bone graft material is placed into the implant socket.
The implant is placed together with the bone graft in the same session or a few months later.
Advantages of Internal Sinus Lift Surgery
It is less invasive and has a shorter recovery period.
It is suitable for patients with mild bone loss.
Crestal Sinus Lift

Crestal Sinus Lift is another method used in the implant placement process and is generally applied to patients with minimal bone height loss. In this technique, the sinus membrane is accessed from the upper part of the implant socket.
Things to Consider After Sinus Lifting Surgery
Things to consider after sinus lifting surgery are important for a smooth recovery process and a successful result.
Medicines
Use antibiotics prescribed by your doctor regularly to prevent the risk of infection.
You can take painkillers recommended by your doctor to control the pain that may occur after surgery.
Mouthwashes: You should ensure your oral hygiene by using antiseptic mouthwashes recommended by your doctor.
Rest and Physical Activity
Rest for the first few days after surgery. Elevating your head while lying down can help reduce swelling and pain.
Avoid heavy exercises and physical activities for the first week after surgery. Avoid lifting weights, bending and sudden movements.
Nutrition
Eat soft and warm foods for the first few days. Avoid hard, spicy, hot or extremely cold foods.
Ensure your body is sufficiently hydrated by drinking plenty of water.
Oral Hygiene
To avoid damaging the surgical area, brush your teeth gently, staying away from the surgery area for the first few days.
Reduce the risk of infection by using antiseptic mouthwashes recommended by your doctor.
Smoking and Drinking Alcohol

Smoking can negatively affect the healing process and increase the risk of infection. You should not smoke after surgery. Alcohol consumption can also negatively affect the healing process. Avoid alcohol consumption after surgery.

Implant applications are a type of dental treatment method applied to replace missing teeth. In some cases, symptoms of failed implants may occur after the implant procedure. Failed implant application may occur due to reasons originating from both the doctor and the patient. Not paying attention to oral care, inadequate bone structure, unhealthy gum tissue, clenching and grinding of teeth, excessive alcohol and smoking are among the patient-related causes of unsuccessful dental implant failure. Reasons caused by the doctor arise based on the doctor’s knowledge and experience. For a successful implant application, the suitability of the patient’s jaw and bone structure, its proximity to the nerve and how the tooth should be positioned should be determined through examination and imaging by the doctor.
What is a Failed Implant?

Dental implant processes are treatments that must be applied with great care. Today, the success rate of implant treatments is over 99%. In order to achieve this success, many factors and many situations must be evaluated and each stage of the treatment must be carried out with great care.

Before implant treatments, teeth and jawbone must be evaluated millimetrically with 3D tomography. The existing jaw bone thickness, length, and proximity to anatomical formations in the area where the implant is planned to be applied must be determined very carefully.

During the implant process, it is very important for the surgical area to be completely sterile for a successful operation. If an implant is placed into the jawbone without paying attention to sterilization, infection will develop around the implant and within the jawbone. In these cases, it is possible to talk about failed implant treatment. In other words, a sterile operating environment reduces the risk of a failed implant process.

After implant operations; Antibiotics, painkillers and mouthwashes are prescribed. It is very important to take antibiotics and mouthwash regularly to prevent infection. You should not smoke for the first two days after the operation, and utmost care should be taken for a week. Otherwise, unsuccessful implant treatment may occur again.

After the dental implant surgery is applied to the jawbone, great dedication is needed in the production phase of implant-supported prostheses. At this stage, the quality of the materials used and the precise work of the dental technician are of great importance in the success of implant procedures. Patients have responsibilities for the long-term success of implant treatments. Paying attention to oral hygiene, regular tooth brushing and dentist visits are the main responsibilities of the patients.
Causes of Failed Implants

Dental implants are a widely used and often successful treatment method to compensate for missing teeth. However, in some cases implants can fail. There are various reasons for these failures. These causes may include many different factors such as biological, mechanical, surgical technique, patient compliance, and environmental factors. Some of the reasons why dental implants fail are as follows:
Surgical Technique and Application Fails
A detailed planning should be made before placing the implant. Poor planning can lead to the implant not being placed in the correct position, resulting in failure.
Non-sterile surgical environment increases the risk of infection. Infections may prevent the implant from adhering.
Incorrect position or angle of the implant within the bone may negatively affect the stability of the implant.
Biological Factors
Bone Insufficiency: Bone in sufficient quantity and quality is required for the implant to hold stably. In case of bone deficiency, osseointegration of the implant cannot be achieved.
Immune Response: The body perceives the implant as a foreign substance and develops an immune response against it, which may also cause the implant to be rejected.
Mechanical Factors
Excessive Pressure: Applying excessive chewing forces to implants can cause the implant to separate from the bone. This situation is especially common when removing single tooth deficiencies.
Prosthesis Incompatibility: Improper design or unsuitability of implant-supported prostheses may cause the implant to carry unbalanced load and cause failure.
Patient Factors
Oral Hygiene: Inadequate oral hygiene increases the risk of peri-implantitis and infection. Good oral hygiene is critical for a long-lasting implant.
Smoking: Smoking is an important factor that negatively affects implant success. The risk of implant loss is higher in patients who smoke.

General Health Status: Systemic diseases such as diabetes and osteoporosis may also affect implant success. In people with such diseases, the healing process may be slow and the risk of infection is increased.
Environmental Factors
Nutritional Habits: Malnutrition can negatively affect bone health and prevent the implant from being stable within the bone.
Traumas: Traumas to the post-surgical area can disrupt the stability of the implant and cause failure.
Raw Material and Design of the Implant
Poor Quality Implant Material: Osseointegration of the implant may fail when low quality or unsuitable materials are used.
Design Problems: The design of the implant can also affect its success. Poorly designed implants cannot adequately integrate with the bone and may be lost.
What are the Symptoms of Failed Implants?

Symptoms of failed implants negatively affect a person’s life. In some cases, when the symptoms are quite severe or the artificial tooth cannot hold, implant treatment is applied again. The most common symptoms of failed implants are as follows:

Long Lasting Severe Pain: It is quite possible to experience pain during the implant application, but if this toothache is severe and does not go away for a long time, it means that there is a problem. Severe pain, for which even the painkillers used after the procedure are not sufficient, can reach unbearable levels for the patient.

Inflammation in the Gum: Swelling may occur after implant application. But if the swelling does not go away and grows, it is understood that it is caused by inflammation as a result of failed implant application.

Displacement of the Implant Tooth: One of the most common symptoms of failed implants is the movement of the implanted tooth. When the movements of the implant tooth are micro-sized, the person may not notice it and it is revealed during the x-ray examination.

Gum Disease: Although gum recession is among the symptoms of failed implants, it can actually occur due to many other reasons. Especially if there is only recession in the gum around the implant, it is understood that it is due to unsuccessful application. If there is not enough bone and gum tissue where the implant is applied, the implant may fail.

Biting and Chewing Problems: After a successful implant surgery, the artificial tooth should function like other teeth and should not cause any problems in biting and chewing. In failed implant applications, difficulty in biting and pain and discomfort during chewing may occur.

If you have tooth loss and are considering implant treatment, you can see our dentists at Dentaliva to find out your suitability for the procedure. Our experienced dentists give you the most accurate and reliable advice for both failed implants and other dental treatments.

### Surgical Technique and Application Fails
A detailed planning should be made before placing the implant. Poor planning can lead to the implant not being placed in the correct position, resulting in failure.
Non-sterile surgical environment increases the risk of infection. Infections may prevent the implant from adhering.
Incorrect position or angle of the implant within the bone may negatively affect the stability of the implant.
### Biological Factors
Bone Insufficiency: Bone in sufficient quantity and quality is required for the implant to hold stably. In case of bone deficiency, osseointegration of the implant cannot be achieved.
Immune Response: The body perceives the implant as a foreign substance and develops an immune response against it, which may also cause the implant to be rejected.
### Mechanical Factors
Excessive Pressure: Applying excessive chewing forces to implants can cause the implant to separate from the bone. This situation is especially common when removing single tooth deficiencies.
Prosthesis Incompatibility: Improper design or unsuitability of implant-supported prostheses may cause the implant to carry unbalanced load and cause failure.
### Patient Factors
Oral Hygiene: Inadequate oral hygiene increases the risk of peri-implantitis and infection. Good oral hygiene is critical for a long-lasting implant.
Smoking: Smoking is an important factor that negatively affects implant success. The risk of implant loss is higher in patients who smoke.

General Health Status: Systemic diseases such as diabetes and osteoporosis may also affect implant success. In people with such diseases, the healing process may be slow and the risk of infection is increased.
### Environmental Factors
Nutritional Habits: Malnutrition can negatively affect bone health and prevent the implant from being stable within the bone.
Traumas: Traumas to the post-surgical area can disrupt the stability of the implant and cause failure.
## Raw Material and Design of the Implant
Poor Quality Implant Material: Osseointegration of the implant may fail when low quality or unsuitable materials are used.
Design Problems: The design of the implant can also affect its success. Poorly designed implants cannot adequately integrate with the bone and may be lost.
## What are the Symptoms of Failed Implants?

Symptoms of failed implants negatively affect a person’s life. In some cases, when the symptoms are quite severe or the artificial tooth cannot hold, implant treatment is applied again. The most common symptoms of failed implants are as follows:

Long Lasting Severe Pain: It is quite possible to experience pain during the implant application, but if this toothache is severe and does not go away for a long time, it means that there is a problem. Severe pain, for which even the painkillers used after the procedure are not sufficient, can reach unbearable levels for the patient.

Inflammation in the Gum: Swelling may occur after implant application. But if the swelling does not go away and grows, it is understood that it is caused by inflammation as a result of failed implant application.

Displacement of the Implant Tooth: One of the most common symptoms of failed implants is the movement of the implanted tooth. When the movements of the implant tooth are micro-sized, the person may not notice it and it is revealed during the x-ray examination.

Gum Disease: Although gum recession is among the symptoms of failed implants, it can actually occur due to many other reasons. Especially if there is only recession in the gum around the implant, it is understood that it is due to unsuccessful application. If there is not enough bone and gum tissue where the implant is applied, the implant may fail.

Biting and Chewing Problems: After a successful implant surgery, the artificial tooth should function like other teeth and should not cause any problems in biting and chewing. In failed implant applications, difficulty in biting and pain and discomfort during chewing may occur.
