Jaw pain is discomfort or pain felt on one or both sides of the jaw. It is one of the most common facial pains. This pain can be caused by a variety of reasons and can often negatively impact quality of life.
Common Causes of Jaw Pain

Temporomandibular Joint (TMJ) Disorders: The jaw joint plays an important role in movements such as chewing and speaking. TMJ can be caused by problems in this joint and can lead to jaw pain. Jaw joint crunching, pain, and chewing are some of the symptoms of these disorders.
Dental Problems: Conditions such as tooth decay, gum disease or teeth clenching can cause jaw pain. These conditions affect the tissues around the teeth and can cause pain.
Sinusitis: Sinusitis is inflammation of the sinuses. It can cause symptoms such as nasal congestion, facial pain and jaw pain.
Stress and Anxiety: Stress and anxiety can cause muscle tension in the body. This may lead to excessive tension of the jaw muscles and jaw pain.
Trauma or Injuries: Damage to the jaw bones as a result of an accident, blow or injury can cause jaw pain. In some cases, it may even be impossible to open your mouth.
Arthritis: Temporomandibular joint arthritis can cause inflammation and pain in the joint.
Muscle Strain: Excessive strain during chewing, speaking, or other jaw movements can cause pain in the muscles that control the jaw. Muscle strain can usually be treated with muscle relaxants.

Trigeminal Neuralgia: The trigeminal nerve carries the sensation of the facial area to the brain. Pain may occur as a result of blood vessels putting pressure on this nerve. Multiple Sclerosis (MS) disease can also cause this condition. Jaw pain seen in trigeminal neuralgia is usually unilateral. This pain, which is felt mostly as upper jaw pain, is often described by patients as like a stabbing or electric shock. Jaw pain caused by trigeminal neuralgia can be so severe that it makes eating and drinking impossible.

Cluster Headache: Cluster headache is a type of pain that begins suddenly or occurs in a specific pattern. This pain can be severe enough to wake the person up at night. Cluster headache can cause pain in the jaw as well as in the eye and temple area.

Osteomyelitis: Infections seen in the bone are called osteomyelitis. Anaerobic osteomyelitis, a subgroup of osteomyelitis, can affect the jawbone. If the bacterial infections in the jawbone are left untreated, permanent damage to the bone may occur.

Tumors and Cysts: Tumors and cysts may occur in the jawbone, soft tissues of the mouth and face. These structures, called odontogenic, are generally not malignant. However, these structures can grow rapidly and affect dental health. Therefore, odontogenic tumors and cysts may need to be removed surgically.
How to Get Rid of Jaw Pain?

In order to answer this question, the condition causing the pain must be determined and treatment planning must be made depending on that condition. The most effective way to determine which of the dozens of jaw pain treatment options will be suitable for you is to find the cause of jaw pain. The most common jaw pain treatments are as follows:
Applying a hot towel to the painful area,
Applying cold on the painful area,
Taking painkillers or muscle relaxants upon doctor’s recommendation,
Massaging the painful jaw joint without applying too much pressure,
Physical therapy practices,
Surgeries for pain caused by accidents and trauma
Jaw Pain Treatment
Jaw pain treatment is applied to the problem causing the pain. If the pain is caused by an infection, antibiotic or antiviral drug treatment can be applied after the doctor’s prescription.

In case of trauma or any structural disorder, surgical treatment can be applied. People who have problems such as teeth grinding or teeth clenching during sleep may be recommended to use night plates or muscle relaxant drug treatments.

Topical ointments containing capsaicin can be used to treat pain caused by nervous disorders, if the doctor deems it necessary. In case of swelling or inflammation in the chin, creams containing steroids can be prescribed by the doctor.

Painkillers help prevent jaw pain in people with migraine and tension-type headaches. However, if the pain is caused by tooth or gum diseases, necessary attention should be paid to oral and dental care and dental treatments for the disease should be performed before it is too late.

In cases where there is no physiological problem causing jaw pain, psychological factors are also taken into consideration. An evaluation is also made from this perspective. In case of psychological disorders, some antidepressant medication and cognitive therapy methods can be applied by a specialist psychiatrist.

Jaw pain can be caused by a variety of reasons and can negatively impact quality of life. Treatment options may vary depending on the specific underlying cause of jaw pain. In addition to all these treatments, a different personalized treatment can also be applied.

Teeth clenching or grinding can be a cause of jaw pain. In this case, a night plate or other oral appliance can be used with dentist advice. Dental health problems, such as tooth decay or gum disease, can cause jaw pain. In this case, appropriate dental treatments can be applied.
Trust Dentaliva for Jaw Pain Treatment

Dentaliva is with you in the treatment of jaw pain. Jaw pain can be caused by a variety of reasons, including temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders, teeth clenching, malocclusion, and stress. In our clinic, by using detailed examination and advanced imaging techniques, we determine the source of the pain and create personalized treatment plans for you. Our treatment methods include physical therapy, oral splints, medication and surgical interventions when necessary. As Dentaliva, we offer the most effective and newest treatment options to relieve your jaw pain and improve your quality of life. You can trust us for a healthy and pain-free life.

Jaw pain caused by trigeminal neuralgia can be so severe that it makes eating and drinking impossible.

Cluster Headache: Cluster headache is a type of pain that begins suddenly or occurs in a specific pattern. This pain can be severe enough to wake the person up at night. Cluster headache can cause pain in the jaw as well as in the eye and temple area.

Osteomyelitis: Infections seen in the bone are called osteomyelitis. Anaerobic osteomyelitis, a subgroup of osteomyelitis, can affect the jawbone. If the bacterial infections in the jawbone are left untreated, permanent damage to the bone may occur.

Tumors and Cysts: Tumors and cysts may occur in the jawbone, soft tissues of the mouth and face. These structures, called odontogenic, are generally not malignant. However, these structures can grow rapidly and affect dental health. Therefore, odontogenic tumors and cysts may need to be removed surgically.
## How to Get Rid of Jaw Pain?

In order to answer this question, the condition causing the pain must be determined and treatment planning must be made depending on that condition. The most effective way to determine which of the dozens of jaw pain treatment options will be suitable for you is to find the cause of jaw pain. The most common jaw pain treatments are as follows:
Applying a hot towel to the painful area,
Applying cold on the painful area,
Taking painkillers or muscle relaxants upon doctor’s recommendation,
Massaging the painful jaw joint without applying too much pressure,
Physical therapy practices,
Surgeries for pain caused by accidents and trauma
## Jaw Pain Treatment
Jaw pain treatment is applied to the problem causing the pain. If the pain is caused by an infection, antibiotic or antiviral drug treatment can be applied after the doctor’s prescription.

In case of trauma or any structural disorder, surgical treatment can be applied. People who have problems such as teeth grinding or teeth clenching during sleep may be recommended to use night plates or muscle relaxant drug treatments.

Topical ointments containing capsaicin can be used to treat pain caused by nervous disorders, if the doctor deems it necessary. In case of swelling or inflammation in the chin, creams containing steroids can be prescribed by the doctor.

Painkillers help prevent jaw pain in people with migraine and tension-type headaches. However, if the pain is caused by tooth or gum diseases, necessary attention should be paid to oral and dental care and dental treatments for the disease should be performed before it is too late.

In cases where there is no physiological problem causing jaw pain, psychological factors are also taken into consideration. An evaluation is also made from this perspective. In case of psychological disorders, some antidepressant medication and cognitive therapy methods can be applied by a specialist psychiatrist.

Jaw pain can be caused by a variety of reasons and can negatively impact quality of life. Treatment options may vary depending on the specific underlying cause of jaw pain. In addition to all these treatments, a different personalized treatment can also be applied.

Teeth clenching or grinding can be a cause of jaw pain. In this case, a night plate or other oral appliance can be used with dentist advice. Dental health problems, such as tooth decay or gum disease, can cause jaw pain. In this case, appropriate dental treatments can be applied.
## Trust Dentaliva for Jaw Pain Treatment

Dentaliva is with you in the treatment of jaw pain. Jaw pain can be caused by a variety of reasons, including temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders, teeth clenching, malocclusion, and stress. In our clinic, by using detailed examination and advanced imaging techniques, we determine the source of the pain and create personalized treatment plans for you. Our treatment methods include physical therapy, oral splints, medication and surgical interventions when necessary. As Dentaliva, we offer the most effective and newest treatment options to relieve your jaw pain and improve your quality of life. You can trust us for a healthy and pain-free life.

As a result of the developments in recent years, implant treatment enables many patients to achieve the smile and aesthetic appearance they desire. The fact that implants have natural tooth function without damaging natural teeth also increases the advantages they offer. As a result of all this, dental implants have become extremely important in oral reconstruction. Implant prostheses are one of the dental aesthetic methods that have been widely used in recent years.
What is Implant Prosthesis?

Fixed or removable dentures placed on and supported by the implant are called implant-supported prostheses. Implant prostheses can be preferred in patients with either a single missing tooth or multiple missing teeth. In other words, there are many patients for whom implant prosthesis can be applied.

Implant prostheses, produced from materials similar to natural teeth, are prostheses with many features that serve to rehabilitate and replace missing teeth. Depending on the patient’s condition, removable or fixed prosthetic rehabilitation can be offered. Both of them enable the removal of missing teeth to repair losses and decreases in chewing and phonatory functions and limit the aesthetic defect. The difference, as the name suggests, is that the removable prosthesis can be removed from the mouth by the patient, while the fixed prosthesis is permanently fixed in the mouth and therefore cannot be removed by the patient on his own.
Implant Prosthesis Types
Implant prosthesis types are divided into fixed implant prostheses and removable implant prostheses.

Implant prostheses that are used permanently by sticking or screwing onto the implant are called fixed prostheses. Implant-supported fixed prostheses, in other words crowns and bridges, can be used for both a single tooth missing and complete jaw edentulism.
Prostheses that are applied on fixed implants placed in people without any teeth and can be inserted and removed by the patient are called removable implant prosthesis or removable dentures.
What is an Implant Fixed Prosthesis?

Implant-supported fixed prostheses allow teeth to be restored using restorations fixed to the patient’s mouth. Implant-supported fixed dentures, also known as indirect restorations, can be used to restore or repair single or multiple teeth. It can also be preferred for restoring small gaps between teeth.

Fixed implant-supported dentures always remain in the patient’s mouth and are placed with surgical procedures. Fixed implant-supported dentures, which are fixed using several dental implants that become an integral part of the jawbone, always remain in the patient’s mouth and cannot be removed.

Implant-supported fixed prostheses are considered ideal especially for people who face deterioration in the gums and jawbone. Bone is a living tissue. It needs constant stimulation to maintain its density and volume. Naturally, this stimulation comes from the teeth, and when it is lost, the bone that surrounds and supports them can begin to break down.

When this situation is not prevented, sagging occurs on the person’s face. Accordingly, an older appearance may occur on the patient’s face. Implant-supported fixed prostheses can stop these negative results and help to have a younger appearance by supporting the facial features provided by the jawbone structure.

Dental implants, which are small screws that function as replacement tooth roots, are placed in the bone just like a natural tooth root. Titanium used in the construction of implants has the ability to fuse with bone through a process called osseointegration.

Implant fixed dentures are artificial teeth that have similar properties to natural teeth, not only aesthetically but also functionally. Fixed implant-supported bridges, which do not slip during eating or speaking, can be used for a long term as proper attention is paid to oral hygiene. They are also known to help prevent bone loss in the jaw.

Implant-supported fixed prostheses offer higher patient satisfaction and success rates than other treatment options. Because there is a significantly reduced mass and no mucosal support is needed, patients can chew more vigorously.

Fixed implant prosthesis can be applied to those who have partial missing teeth, those who have lost all their teeth, those whose teeth are spaced out, those who have physical and chemical wear on their teeth, and those who will undergo smile design.
Bridges or individual crown-shaped crowns are attached to the implants with screws or special adhesives, ensuring that they remain stable in the mouth and function like the patient’s own teeth.

Fixed implant prostheses offer aesthetics and comfortable use. Implant-supported fixed dentures, which look and feel like natural teeth, become integral parts of the jawbone after the procedure is completed.

This method, in which the prosthesis is attached to the abutment fixed on the implant with special adhesives, offers more aesthetic results in anterior group restorations. Since there is no screw hole on the prosthesis and the abutment can be produced individually, aesthetic problems that may be caused by implant angulation problems can be prevented. Since porcelain and metal are integrated as a whole, problems such as porcelain fractures are prevented.
What is an Implant Removable Prosthesis?

For many people who do not have teeth in one or both jaws, removable dentures are an economical way to restore their smile. However, dentures are not always easy to fit. They can easily slip out of place while eating or talking. One of the most effective methods that can be preferred to prevent problems that may arise from this situation is to support removable dentures with dental implants.

Dental implants are considered lifelike replacements for individual missing teeth. Although dental implants are one of the most useful methods for people who have most of their natural teeth, it is not a preferred method to install a dental implant for each missing tooth in patients who have no teeth left in one or both jaws. The preferred effective solution is to place at least two dental implants in the jaw to support a removable denture so that it does not come loose when inserted.

Dental implants are small titanium screws that serve the same purpose as the roots of natural teeth. Like natural tooth roots, they are located below the gum line and are not visible in the mouth. In addition, they ensure that the teeth that replace the natural teeth are fixed to the jawbone. Dental implants become part of the gum tissue because titanium has the unique ability to fuse to living bone. When fixed with a prosthesis implant, it does not put destructive pressure on bone tissue.

The United Kingdom is home to world-renowned dental clinics and experienced dentists for dental treatments. Dental clinics in the UK have high quality standards and are regularly inspected. State-of-the-art equipment and methods are used in UK dental clinics. Dentists have a wide range of education and practical experience. Dentists graduate from internationally recognized training programs.
Education and Experience of Dentists in the UK

In the United Kingdom, dentists generally train at university dental faculties. The training process consists of theoretical and practical training and usually lasts 5 years. In the UK, dentists can specialize in certain areas. For example, they can receive specialized training in different fields such as oral surgery, pedodontics, endodontics and periodontology. After graduation, dentists often complete clinical internships and continue their education to specialize in specific areas.
In the UK, dentists are subject to ongoing training and supervision throughout their careers. This allows dentists to stay informed about current and new dental treatment processes and technologies.
Dental Treatments Provided in Dental Clinics in the United Kingdom
The United Kingdom is one of the leading countries in dental health, with cutting edge technology and up-to-date treatment methods.
1. General Dental Examination and Cleaning

Dental clinics in the UK offer comprehensive dental examinations to protect, treat and improve patients’ oral and dental health. Generally, the first examination is performed to evaluate the patient’s general oral and dental health condition, identify possible problems and create a treatment plan. During this examination, the dentist may perform a variety of diagnostic tests, such as intraoral examination, dental x-rays, and other imaging methods when necessary. This comprehensive examination process is customized to patients’ individual needs and health history so that the most appropriate and effective treatment plan can be created. Dental clinics in the UK are equipped with modern technology and up-to-date treatment methods, allowing them to provide patients with high-quality and professional dental examination services.

Dental cleaning is a dental treatment procedure performed routinely to maintain dental health and emphasize the importance of oral hygiene. During this procedure, the dentist uses a special tool and technique to remove plaque and tartar accumulated on the teeth. Additionally, it smoothes tooth surfaces and removes debris between teeth. The advantages of dental cleaning include preventing tooth decay and gum diseases, reducing bad breath, making teeth appear whiter and brighter, and protecting general oral and dental health. This procedure is performed in a hygienic environment by trained professionals in dental clinics and is generally a painless process. Regular dental cleaning is an important step to protect individuals’ oral and dental care.
2. Restorative Treatments

Composite dental fillings are popular filling options that offer aesthetics and functionality together. These fillings are in natural tooth color and texture and provide an aesthetic that is compatible with the tooth color. Composite fillings consist of a mixture of glass and resin particles and are prepared so that the dentist can apply them directly to the tooth. During application, the composite material is poured into the tooth cavity in liquid form and hardened with a special light. These fillings are used to treat small and medium-sized caries, repair fractures or cracks in teeth, and correct tooth shape. Its advantages include providing an aesthetic appearance, being compatible with tooth color, and being a minimally invasive treatment method. However, composite fillings may be less durable than metal fillings and may discolor over time. With proper care and regular dentist checks, composite fillings can provide a long-lasting and effective solution.

They are used on the back teeth as they are more durable. Amalgam dental fillings are an old and effective filling option created by combining a metallic mixture of silver, mercury, copper and other metals. These fillings are renowned for their strength and durability and are often used on the back parts of the teeth, especially on the chewing surfaces. Amalgam fillings require a certain amount of time to complete the hardening process, and it is recommended to avoid chewing load during this period so that the filling reaches full hardness. Since amalgam is blue-black or silver in color, they are not as aesthetically preferred as composite fillings, but they are still preferred by many dentists due to their durability and cost effectiveness. The advantages of amalgam fillings include their longevity, good resistance to chewing forces, and cost-effectiveness. However, there is concern that they may cause allergic reactions or sensitivities in some people due to the mercury they contain.

Porcelain dental fillings are one of the filling options that offer aesthetic results closest to the natural tooth color and tissue structure. These fillings are durable and long-lasting and are used to perfectly repair tooth decay, fractures or aesthetic problems. Porcelain fillings are specially prepared in a laboratory environment and placed appropriately in the teeth by the dentist.
3. Orthodontic Treatments

In the United Kingdom, orthodontic treatments are widely preferred to bring the teeth and jaw into the correct position and achieve an aesthetic smile. In the United Kingdom, orthodontic treatments are usually offered under the NHS (National Health Service), but individuals can also receive this service in private clinics. Although the treatment process usually varies depending on individual needs, most orthodontic treatments can last from a few months to a few years.
4. Dental Implants

Dental implant procedures in the UK are an extremely popular and effective method of treating missing teeth. Dental implants are placed in the jawbone with a screw-shaped structure made of titanium and fuse with the bone, creating a solid and durable base. The implant treatment process consists of several stages, including implant placement, healing process and prosthesis application, and can usually take several months. During this process, patients need to have regular check-ups and pay attention to their oral hygiene.
Dental Treatment Cost in the UK

Dental treatment costs in the UK vary depending on the type of service provided, materials used and the fee policy of the clinic or specialist performing the treatment. Fees for basic dental treatments, such as tooth extractions, fillings or scaling, are usually within a fixed price range, with standard charges set by the NHS (National Health Service). On the other hand, prices may be higher for more specialized services such as cosmetic dental treatments, implants or orthodontic treatments. Treatment fees at private dental clinics may vary depending on the location, expertise and service quality of the clinics. The cost of dental treatments in the UK is usually paid out of patients’ pocket, although in certain cases NHS treatment fees may be covered for some or all of the cost. Before starting treatment, it is recommended that patients obtain detailed information about the treatment plan and cost.

The United Kingdom is home to world-renowned dental clinics and experienced dentists for dental treatments. Dental clinics in the UK have high quality standards and are regularly inspected. State-of-the-art equipment and methods are used in UK dental clinics. Dentists have a wide range of education and practical experience. Dentists graduate from internationally recognized training programs.
## Education and Experience of Dentists in the UK

In the United Kingdom, dentists generally train at university dental faculties. The training process consists of theoretical and practical training and usually lasts 5 years. In the UK, dentists can specialize in certain areas. For example, they can receive specialized training in different fields such as oral surgery, pedodontics, endodontics and periodontology. After graduation, dentists often complete clinical internships and continue their education to specialize in specific areas.
In the UK, dentists are subject to ongoing training and supervision throughout their careers. This allows dentists to stay informed about current and new dental treatment processes and technologies.
## Dental Treatments Provided in Dental Clinics in the United Kingdom
The United Kingdom is one of the leading countries in dental health, with cutting edge technology and up-to-date treatment methods.
### 1. General Dental Examination and Cleaning

Dental clinics in the UK offer comprehensive dental examinations to protect, treat and improve patients’ oral and dental health. Generally, the first examination is performed to evaluate the patient’s general oral and dental health condition, identify possible problems and create a treatment plan. During this examination, the dentist may perform a variety of diagnostic tests, such as intraoral examination, dental x-rays, and other imaging methods when necessary. This comprehensive examination process is customized to patients’ individual needs and health history so that the most appropriate and effective treatment plan can be created. Dental clinics in the UK are equipped with modern technology and up-to-date treatment methods, allowing them to provide patients with high-quality and professional dental examination services.

Dental cleaning is a dental treatment procedure performed routinely to maintain dental health and emphasize the importance of oral hygiene. During this procedure, the dentist uses a special tool and technique to remove plaque and tartar accumulated on the teeth. Additionally, it smoothes tooth surfaces and removes debris between teeth. The advantages of dental cleaning include preventing tooth decay and gum diseases, reducing bad breath, making teeth appear whiter and brighter, and protecting general oral and dental health. This procedure is performed in a hygienic environment by trained professionals in dental clinics and is generally a painless process. Regular dental cleaning is an important step to protect individuals’ oral and dental care.
### 2. Restorative Treatments

Composite dental fillings are popular filling options that offer aesthetics and functionality together. These fillings are in natural tooth color and texture and provide an aesthetic that is compatible with the tooth color. Composite fillings consist of a mixture of glass and resin particles and are prepared so that the dentist can apply them directly to the tooth. During application, the composite material is poured into the tooth cavity in liquid form and hardened with a special light. These fillings are used to treat small and medium-sized caries, repair fractures or cracks in teeth, and correct tooth shape. Its advantages include providing an aesthetic appearance, being compatible with tooth color, and being a minimally invasive treatment method. However, composite fillings may be less durable than metal fillings and may discolor over time. With proper care and regular dentist checks, composite fillings can provide a long-lasting and effective solution.

They are used on the back teeth as they are more durable. Amalgam dental fillings are an old and effective filling option created by combining a metallic mixture of silver, mercury, copper and other metals. These fillings are renowned for their strength and durability and are often used on the back parts of the teeth, especially on the chewing surfaces. Amalgam fillings require a certain amount of time to complete the hardening process, and it is recommended to avoid chewing load during this period so that the filling reaches full hardness. Since amalgam is blue-black or silver in color, they are not as aesthetically preferred as composite fillings, but they are still preferred by many dentists due to their durability and cost effectiveness. The advantages of amalgam fillings include their longevity, good resistance to chewing forces, and cost-effectiveness. However, there is concern that they may cause allergic reactions or sensitivities in some people due to the mercury they contain.

Porcelain dental fillings are one of the filling options that offer aesthetic results closest to the natural tooth color and tissue structure. These fillings are durable and long-lasting and are used to perfectly repair tooth decay, fractures or aesthetic problems. Porcelain fillings are specially prepared in a laboratory environment and placed appropriately in the teeth by the dentist.
### 3. Orthodontic Treatments

In the United Kingdom, orthodontic treatments are widely preferred to bring the teeth and jaw into the correct position and achieve an aesthetic smile. In the United Kingdom, orthodontic treatments are usually offered under the NHS (National Health Service), but individuals can also receive this service in private clinics. Although the treatment process usually varies depending on individual needs, most orthodontic treatments can last from a few months to a few years.
### 4. Dental Implants

Dental implant procedures in the UK are an extremely popular and effective method of treating missing teeth. Dental implants are placed in the jawbone with a screw-shaped structure made of titanium and fuse with the bone, creating a solid and durable base. The implant treatment process consists of several stages, including implant placement, healing process and prosthesis application, and can usually take several months. During this process, patients need to have regular check-ups and pay attention to their oral hygiene.
## Dental Treatment Cost in the UK

Dental treatment costs in the UK vary depending on the type of service provided, materials used and the fee policy of the clinic or specialist performing the treatment. Fees for basic dental treatments, such as tooth extractions, fillings or scaling, are usually within a fixed price range, with standard charges set by the NHS (National Health Service). On the other hand, prices may be higher for more specialized services such as cosmetic dental treatments, implants or orthodontic treatments. Treatment fees at private dental clinics may vary depending on the location, expertise and service quality of the clinics. The cost of dental treatments in the UK is usually paid out of patients’ pocket, although in certain cases NHS treatment fees may be covered for some or all of the cost. Before starting treatment, it is recommended that patients obtain detailed information about the treatment plan and cost.

When to Get Dental Crowns

Dental crowns are caps placed over teeth that are damaged, decayed, or appear aesthetically pleasing. Crowns provide both functional and aesthetic improvement by re-creating the natural structure of the tooth. They are usually made using porcelain, ceramic, metal alloy, or a combination of these. One of the most frequently asked questions about dental crowns is “When to get dental crowns.” Dental crowns are an effective method used in the treatment of various dental problems. However, many factors must be taken into consideration when a dental crown is required. The most common situations where a dental crown is required are as follows:
Damaged Teeth

Broken or Cracked Teeth: Fractures or cracks may occur in natural teeth as a result of trauma, accidents or excessive teeth grinding. In this case, a dental crown may be required to restore the function and aesthetics of the tooth.
Severely Decayed Teeth: Dental crowns can be used for restorative treatment in badly decayed teeth.
Replacement of Large Fillings: Crowns are suitable to preserve the structure of the tooth in cases of large cavities or where old fillings have failed.
Aesthetic Fixes
Color Changes: Porcelain or ceramic crowns may be preferred for color changes that cannot be achieved with tooth whitening procedures.
Shape or Size Changes: Crowns can be applied for aesthetic purposes in case of tooth shape and size disorders that are congenital or occur as a result of accidents.
Dental Implants
The function and aesthetics of the missing tooth are completed with crowns placed on the dental implants applied to replace the missing teeth.
Supporting and Placement of Dental Bridges
In cases of missing teeth, dental crowns may be needed to support and securely position bridges.
Protecting the Structure of the Tooth

There may be wear on the structure of the tooth due to reasons such as excessive teeth grinding, incorrect tooth brushing technique or excessive consumption of acidic foods. In this case, dental crowns can be used to protect the structure of the tooth.
After Root Canal Treatment
After root canal treatment, the tooth structure becomes weak and sensitive. In such cases, a crown is suitable to increase the strength and durability of the tooth.
What Materials Are Dental Crowns Made From?

A dental crown is used to recreate the original shape of a fixed prosthesis to cover the treated tooth after a tooth trauma or fracture. The internal structure of the dental crown is made of zirconium, metal or reshaped ceramic. Its outer structure is made of valuable alloys such as gold, platinum and chrome-cobalt, or resin or ceramics.
Zirconium Dental Crown

Zirconium dental crown is an effective solution to restore and replace missing teeth. While the outer part is made of ceramic, zirconium is used in the inner structure to give strength to the prosthesis. This type of prosthesis has a very high resistance and an aesthetic appearance that cannot be compared to any other material. Zirconium crowns are lighter and more durable than metal-ceramic crowns.
Ceramic Dental Crown

A ceramic crown consists of two parts: the inner structure made of metal or the outer part made of precious metal alloys as mentioned above. This type of prosthesis is very durable and fits well with the patient’s tooth structure. It is also successful in terms of aesthetics.
How Are Dental Crowns Applied? What are the Stages of Dental Crown Treatment?
Dental crowns are performed by dentists in several stages:
Stage 1: The damaged natural crown is removed, the tooth is then filed and some of the enamel is removed to create the necessary space.

Stage 2: At this stage, the dentist takes dental measurements. A mold of the tooth is then sent to a special laboratory and then used to create a perfect veneer in the shape of natural teeth. At this stage, a temporary dental crown made of acrylic resin is applied.

Stage 3: Before the last step, the dentist evaluates the shape, size and color of the new crown together with the patient. To have a perfect smile again, the crown must be the same shape, size and color as natural teeth.

Stage 4: The final veneer will be permanently fixed by the dentist as soon as it is tested on the patient. Once the crown is ready, it is tested so it can be touched up or replaced before it is permanently fixed.
Things to Know After Crown Treatment
Crown treatment is basically divided into two: temporary crown and permanent crown. There are things to pay attention to after both of these procedures.
Temporary Crowns

Temporary crowns are more fragile. Therefore, you should take extra care of your temporary crown. After the temporary crown is attached, do not eat anything for at least 30 minutes to allow the bonding material to dry. In particular, it is important to avoid chewing gum and eating hard or sticky foods. In the following days, take care to chew as much as possible on the opposite side where the crown is placed. Brush your teeth gently and do not floss directly around the temporary crown.
Permanent Crowns

It is important that you avoid eating hard and sticky foods or chewing gum for the first 24 hours after the permanent dental crown is placed. You can brush your teeth, but you should floss very carefully during the healing period. Your gums may be sore for the first few days following the dental crown procedure. In this case, your dentist will recommend painkillers.
How to Extend the Life of a Dental Crown?
As a procedure, having a dental crown for a longer period of time is similar to taking care of your own teeth.
Pay attention to oral hygiene. Brush your teeth after every meal.
Stay away from alcoholic beverages.
Reduce consumption of sugary foods and drinks.

Each patient’s tooth structure, aesthetic preferences and needs are different. At Dentaliva, personalized dental crown treatment plans are prepared in accordance with the individual needs and expectations of our patients.

Dental Implant Technology in Turkey

Turkey stands out internationally regarding dental implant treatments not only with its affordable costs, but also with implant brands that closely follow and apply the latest technology. Dental implant brands in Turkey closely follow technological developments in the world and apply the latest innovations and technologies in their treatments.

Dental implant clinics in Turkey are equipped with state-of-the-art devices and equipment. State-of-the-art devices such as 3D dental tomography, digital x-ray and digital planning enable patients to have a faster, more comfortable and more effective treatment experience during the treatment process. Another important reason why dental implant technology is so advanced in Turkey is the country’s continuous education and research activities on dental implant treatments. Dentists in Turkey regularly participate in international training programs and learn and apply the latest technological and scientific developments in dental implant treatments.
Types of Dental Implant Treatment Applied in Turkey
Dental implant treatments in Turkey are carried out with a series of treatment methods diversified according to different needs and situations. Some of these methods are as follows:

One-Stage Implant Treatment: In one-stage implant treatment, the implant is placed directly under the gum and a temporary or permanent prosthesis is immediately attached to it. This method shortens the healing process of the implant and accelerates the treatment process.

Two-Stage Implant Treatment: In the two-stage implant treatment, the implant is placed in the jawbone in the first stage and covered. In the second stage, the prosthesis is attached to the implant. This method requires waiting for the implant to fuse well with the bone, but it is preferred to achieve successful results in the long term.

All-on-4/All-on-6 Treatment: All-on-4 or All-on-6 treatment is a fixed bridge application for missing teeth. In this method, all upper or lower teeth are supported by a fixed bridge using 4 or 6 implants. This treatment method offers an effective and fast solution for complex tooth deficiencies.

Sinus Lifting and Grafting: In cases where the jawbone is insufficient, surgical procedures such as sinus lifting and grafting can be performed before implant placement. These procedures are performed to strengthen the jawbone and increase bone volume for successful placement of the implant.

Zirconium Implants: As an alternative to traditional titanium implants, aesthetic and biocompatible zirconium implants are also preferred in Turkey. Zirconium implants are an option that has no risk of allergy and provides a natural tooth appearance.

How to Clean Between Teeth?

Healthy oral hygiene starts not only with cleaning the tooth surfaces, but also with effectively cleaning between the teeth. Because cleaning plaque and debris between teeth helps prevent caries and gum problems. So, how to clean between teeth? There are several methods of cleaning the spaces between teeth.
Using an Interdental Brush

Interdental brushes are an ideal cleaning tool for large spaces between teeth and for people using braces. Carefully place the interdental brush between the teeth and gently move it to remove plaque and debris. There are different sizes and shapes of interdental brushes, so you should choose the one that suits your needs. If you are going to use an interdental brush for the first time, you can start with the smallest size.
Flossing

Dental floss is a material made of thin thread or nylon used to clean debris and plaque between the teeth. Flossing is important to protect teeth and gum health as a complement to tooth brushing. It helps prevent caries and gum diseases by cleaning food residues and plaque accumulated between narrow teeth where the toothbrush cannot reach. Additionally, regular flossing strengthens gums, prevents bad breath and makes teeth look whiter and brighter. Therefore, it is important to floss regularly as part of a oral heealth care routine.
How to Use Dental Floss
Take a piece of dental floss about 45cm long.
Leave a space of approximately 5-7 cm in the middle of the floss by wrapping both ends around your middle fingers.
Gently put the floss between the two teeth. The floss should move below the gum.
The floss should touch both surfaces.
After cleaning, gently remove the floss.
Throw away used dental floss and never reuse it.
Things to Consider When Using Dental Floss
Use dental floss gently to avoid damaging the gums. Avoid applying excessive force and pressure.
Place the floss under the gum and move it towards the lateral surface of the tooth. Do not pull the floss too hard or you may injure your gums.
First, brush your teeth and then floss. This helps clean teeth more effectively because dental floss reaches areas that a regular toothbrush cannot reach and provides a detailed clean.
Prevent bacteria from being carried between teeth by using a new section for each interdental space. Thus, you can also prevent gum inflammation.

There are several different types of dental floss. These are waxed dental floss, wax-free dental floss, thick floss and thin floss. Among these types, you should choose the most suitable type for you.
If you have any questions or concerns about flossing, ask your dentist or dental hygienist for advice.
Water Spraying Devices (Oral Irrigator)

Water spray devices are used to clean plaque and debris between teeth with a water jet. These devices are an ideal alternative, especially for people who find flossing difficult. When using an oral irrigator, it is important to start on a low pressure setting and be careful to avoid damaging the gums.

An oral irrigator is an electronic device used to clean plaque, food debris and bacteria between teeth with jets of water and air. Oral irrigators are considered an effective oral hygiene tool that complements the use of a toothbrush and dental floss. Water and air jets thoroughly clean the areas between the teeth and gums, providing a fresh and clean feeling inside the mouth.
If this is your first time using an oral irrigator, it is important to use it at low pressure. You can increase the pressure over time, but be careful not to injure your gums.
Try to provide the most effective cleaning by holding the head of the oral irrigator at the right angle to the teeth and gums.
Use the oral irrigator at least once a day, preferably before going to bed. This helps you maintain your oral hygiene.
Rinse the water tank with clean water after each use and clean it regularly.
If you have any questions or concerns about using an oral irrigator, ask your dentist or dental hygienist for advice.
Professional Teeth Cleaning

Professional teeth cleaning is a dental health procedure performed by dentists. During this procedure, hard plaque (tartar) and stains accumulated on the teeth are cleaned by dentists. Everyone should have professional teeth cleaning at least twice a year. Because even though all home dental cleaning processes are done regularly and carefully, they may not be sufficient to remove plaque.

Dental İmplants In Istanbul

Dental implants in Istanbul have revolutionized modern dentistry, offering a permanent solution for missing teeth and restoring both function and aesthetics to the smile. Istanbul, the vibrant metropolis bridging Europe and Asia, has emerged as a prime destination for dental implant procedures. There are several compelling reasons why opting for dental implant treatment in Istanbul can be advantageous, particularly in terms of cost-effectiveness compared to other European countries.
Advantages of Dental Implant Treatment in Istanbul
Dental implant treatment in Istanbul has many advantages. These advantages are as follows:

One of the most significant advantages of getting dental implants in Istanbul is the competitive pricing offered by dental clinics throughout the city. Compared to many European countries, including those in Western Europe, the cost of dental implants in Istanbul is notably lower. This affordability stems from various factors, including lower operating costs for dental clinics.

In Istanbul, the cost of labor, including dental professionals’ salaries and wages, tends to be more reasonable compared to European countries. This difference in labor costs directly influences the overall pricing of dental implant procedures, making Istanbul an attractive option for individuals seeking high-quality dental care at a fraction of the cost they might incur elsewhere.

Despite the lower implant costs in Turkey, dental clinics in Istanbul boast state-of-the-art facilities equipped with the latest advancements in dental technology. Patients can expect to receive top-quality dental care in modern, well-equipped clinics that adhere to international standards of hygiene and safety.

Istanbul is home to a vast pool of highly qualified and experienced dental professionals who specialize in implant dentistry. Many dentists in Istanbul have received training and accreditation from prestigious institutions both domestically and internationally. Patients can rest assured knowing that their dental implant procedure will be performed by skilled professionals with a wealth of expertise in the field.

Choosing Istanbul for dental implant treatment offers the opportunity to immerse oneself in a rich cultural experience. With its captivating blend of history, architecture, and cuisine, Istanbul provides a unique backdrop for dental care that can turn a routine procedure into a memorable journey.
There are dozens of implant brands in Istanbul that produce both in Turkey and in European countries. These implant brands produce high quality products.
Dental Implant Procedure

Implant dental treatment in Istanbul is completed in stages. However, two different methods are used in implant treatment. The first of these methods is to place the new tooth immediately after the patient’s tooth is extracted, that is, without a waiting period. In the other method, treatment is interrupted for 1 to 3 months after tooth extraction. The purpose of taking a break from treatment is to ensure optimal fusion of the bone and the implant.
Initial Examination and Treatment Planning

One of the most important steps in implant treatment is determining the patient’s suitability for treatment and planning the treatment correctly. At this stage, the patient is examined in detail. The condition of the gums, lower and upper jaw, teeth and whether each of these elements is suitable for implant treatment are checked. After the inspection, the planning process begins. Detailed planning is made, such as how many implants will be used, the structure of the implants to be used, and the type of dental prosthesis to be made. Performing this step correctly is very important to get the best result from the treatment.

The examination is basically performed to understand whether the patient’s jawbone is suitable and sufficient for implant treatment. Some people’s jawbone may not be sufficient for implant treatment. In this case, it is not possible for the bone to hold the implant root. In cases where there is not enough bone, additional procedures such as bone graft treatment may be required.

Implant surgery is planned by dentists in the most appropriate way for the patient. Before starting the operation, local anesthesia is applied to the teeth and jaw area. Using appropriate surgical instruments, the slots where the implant will be placed are opened and the implants are placed.

In the stitched implant procedure, an incision is made in the gum and screws are applied after reaching the bone. After the implant is placed, the incision is closed with stitches and the procedure is completed. Situations such as completion of the operation process and the number of implants may change.
After the implant is placed, it is necessary to wait for the jawbone to fuse with the implant. During this period, dental care should be taken to prevent infection of the tooth roots
Treatment of Dental Implant Problems

Dental implants are a great way to restore missing or failing teeth. However, as with any treatment, there can sometimes be problems or complications. Despite the many advantages a dental implant offers, problems can arise, especially in patients with poor oral hygiene, heavy smokers, or if the dental implant treatment has not been performed optimally.
If the treatment is performed by experienced clinicians and the patient takes proper care of their mouth, there are very few possible problems with dental implants.

One of the problems in dental implant treatment is gum recession at the implant. This can occur if the implant is placed incorrectly or if there is insufficient bone or gum around the implant, especially on the facial side.
Additionally, you may be more susceptible to problems or complications with dental implant treatment if you have any of the following:
Insufficient healthy jaw bone and unsuitability for bone grafting,
Medical conditions such as cancer, diabetes, or AIDS that affect your body’s ability to heal itself
Any condition that affects your ability to clean your teeth well, i.e. use your hands and arms,

As a result, dental implants in Istanbul are much more advantageous than many countries in terms of both quality and price. There are several compelling reasons why opting for dental implant treatment in Istanbul can be advantageous, particularly in terms of cost-effectiveness compared to other European countries.
## Advantages of Dental Implant Treatment in Istanbul
Dental implant treatment in Istanbul has many advantages. These advantages are as follows:

One of the most significant advantages of getting dental implants in Istanbul is the competitive pricing offered by dental clinics throughout the city. Istanbul is home to a vast pool of highly qualified and experienced dental professionals who specialize in implant dentistry. Many dentists in Istanbul have received training and accreditation from prestigious institutions both domestically and internationally. Patients can rest assured knowing that their dental implant procedure will be performed by skilled professionals with a wealth of expertise in the field.

Choosing Istanbul for dental implant treatment offers the opportunity to immerse oneself in a rich cultural experience. With its captivating blend of history, architecture, and cuisine, Istanbul provides a unique backdrop for dental care that can turn a routine procedure into a memorable journey.
There are dozens of implant brands in Istanbul that produce both in Turkey and in European countries. These implant brands produce high quality products.
## Dental Implant Procedure

Implant dental treatment in Istanbul is completed in stages. However, two different methods are used in implant treatment. The first of these methods is to place the new tooth immediately after the patient’s tooth is extracted, that is, without a waiting period. In the other method, treatment is interrupted for 1 to 3 months after tooth extraction. The purpose of taking a break from treatment is to ensure optimal fusion of the bone and the implant.
### Initial Examination and Treatment Planning

One of the most important steps in implant treatment is determining the patient’s suitability for treatment and planning the treatment correctly. At this stage, the patient is examined in detail. The condition of the gums, lower and upper jaw, teeth and whether each of these elements is suitable for implant treatment are checked. After the inspection, the planning process begins. Detailed planning is made, such as how many implants will be used, the structure of the implants to be used, and the type of dental prosthesis to be made. Performing this step correctly is very important to get the best result from the treatment.

The examination is basically performed to understand whether the patient’s jawbone is suitable and sufficient for implant treatment. Some people’s jawbone may not be sufficient for implant treatment. In this case, it is not possible for the bone to hold the implant root. In cases where there is not enough bone, additional procedures such as bone graft treatment may be required.

Implant surgery is planned by dentists in the most appropriate way for the patient. Before starting the operation, local anesthesia is applied to the teeth and jaw area. Using appropriate surgical instruments, the slots where the implant will be placed are opened and the implants are placed.

In the stitched implant procedure, an incision is made in the gum and screws are applied after reaching the bone. After the implant is placed, the incision is closed with stitches and the procedure is completed. Situations such as completion of the operation process and the number of implants may change.
After the implant is placed, it is necessary to wait for the jawbone to fuse with the implant. During this period, dental care should be taken to prevent infection of the tooth roots
## Treatment of Dental Implant Problems

Dental implants are a great way to restore missing or failing teeth. However, as with any treatment, there can sometimes be problems or complications. Despite the many advantages a dental implant offers, problems can arise, especially in patients with poor oral hygiene, heavy smokers, or if the dental implant treatment has not been performed optimally.
If the treatment is performed by experienced clinicians and the patient takes proper care of their mouth, there are very few possible problems with dental implants.

One of the problems in dental implant treatment is gum recession at the implant. This can occur if the implant is placed incorrectly or if there is insufficient bone or gum around the implant, especially on the facial side.
Additionally, you may be more susceptible to problems or complications with dental implant treatment if you have any of the following:
Insufficient healthy jaw bone and unsuitability for bone grafting,
Medical conditions such as cancer, diabetes, or AIDS that affect your body’s ability to heal itself
Any condition that affects your ability to clean your teeth well, i.e. use your hands and arms,

As a result, dental implants in Istanbul are much more advantageous than many countries in terms of both quality and price. Thanks to the agreements made by dental clinics in Istanbul with international insurance companies, you can have your implant treatments and other dental treatments in Istanbul at very affordable prices with the comfort of a holiday.
Dentaliva can offer you all these opportunities. Contact us for our dental implants and other dental treatments in Istanbul.

Composite Veneers in Turkey

There are important developments in the field of dental aesthetics in Turkey. Composite veneers in Turkey are one of these developments and offer an ideal solution for many people with aesthetic concerns. Dentists in Turkey use modern techniques to provide their patients with natural and attractive smiles with developed dental procedures.

Composite dental veneers in Turkey are made in colors close to the natural tooth color and are shaped by dentists to suit the patient’s tooth structure. This makes the veneer look natural and compatible with the teeth. Dentists in Turkey work meticulously to maximize patient satisfaction and provide personalized solutions for each patient.
The materials used in composite coatings are resin-based.

Composite coatings can be used for 5 years or longer. Composite veneers can be prepared in a laboratory environment or applied directly to the teeth in the mouth by dentists. It cannot be easily distinguished from other teeth. Composite fillings shorten the treatment time because they can often be applied in a single session.
Advantages of Composite Veneers in Turkey
Composite veneers treatment in Turkey has many advantages. These advantages are as follows:
Composite dental veneers in Turkey are offered at more affordable prices compared to other European countries.
Treatment costs are generally lower, providing solutions that fit patients’ budgets.
Turkey is a popular tourism destination around the world with its historical and touristic values.

Vacation can be combined with dental treatment. Patients can discover the unique beauties of Turkey and enjoy their holiday while receiving their treatments such as such as teeth whitening, dental implants and composite veneers.
Dentist in Turkey are trained and experienced professionals in accordance with international standards.
They follow technological developments in the healthcare sector and apply the latest techniques.
Dental clinics in Turkey have modern medical devices and high-quality materials to offer personalized and best dental treatment to their patients.
Stages of Composite Dental Veneer Treatment

Among dental aesthetic treatment applications, composite laminate veneers are one of the most comfortable restorations for the dentist and the patient. The stages of this dental procedure, which can usually be completed in a single session, are as follows:

Examination and determination of suitability for composite laminate veneer treatment: Intraoral examination determines the suitability of composite laminate veneer. There are certain conditions for this treatment to be performed. If these conditions are not suitable, the treatment may fail.

Choosing the appropriate color for composite laminates: Although the dentist’s guidance on color is important, the patient’s preference is more important. That’s why our experienced dentists always take into account their patients’ wishes regarding veneer colors.

Abrasion procedures (preparation) that need to be done on the teeth: If there is any decay on the tooth or teeth to be made of composite lamimate, they are cleaned. Dark colored areas that cannot be covered with composite material may be removed. Protruding and long areas that may interfere with the newly planned tooth forms are smoothed.

Bonding: The teeth to be treated are washed and cleaned. If there are any stains on the teeth and decay particles after abrasion, they are removed. To prevent the teeth from getting uncontrolledly wet during the application, they are insulated with cotton rolls or special materials for this purpose. Chemical etching is applied followed by bonding that connects the tooth and the filling material. Composite veneer restorations should only adhere to the relevant tooth. Small transparent nylon leaves are placed between the teeth to prevent it from overflowing and sticking to the adjacent teeth. These leaves are removed after the process.

Application of composite material: It is the process of placing composite material selected in appropriate color on prepared tooth surfaces. The process is completed by placing the composite, which can be matte and transparent, on the tooth surface in layers, shaping it and hardening it with a suitable light source.
Dental Composite Veneer Cost in Turkey

Dental composite veneers are a frequently preferred method to aesthetically correct and beautify teeth. There are various factors as to why dental composite veneer prices are affordable in Turkey. These factors are as follows.

Material Costs: The cost of materials used for dental composite veneers in Turkey is generally lower than in other countries. This directly affects the cost of the coating process and enables more affordable prices to be offered.

Dental Tourism: Turkey has become popular for dental tourism in recent years. High quality dental services and affordable prices attract foreign patients to Turkey. This increases the competitive environment and makes prices more affordable.

Competence of Dentists and Competition: There are many talented dentists in Turkey. This helps increase competition and keep prices reasonable. Additionally, the education level and experience of dentists affect prices by reducing labor costs.

Low Labor and Operating Costs: Labor costs in Turkey are lower compared to some Western countries. Dentists and clinics generally have lower operating costs, which affects treatment costs. For example, the rent of a clinic building is much more affordable than in European countries. Also, owning a property in Turkey is much easier than in other countries. This makes it easier for businesses to operate in their own buildings. This is a factor that directly affects operating costs.

Local Production and Supply Chain: Production or import of dental materials can be provided from local sources. This contributes to the reduction of logistics costs and therefore the low prices of dental treatments in Turkey.

Insurance Coverage and Payment Options: Many dental clinics in Turkey have various insurance plans and payment options. This allows patients to cover treatment costs more easily and benefit from more affordable prices.

When all these factors come together, it can be more clearly understood why dental composite veneer prices in Turkey are affordable. However, one of the most important factors in determining prices is the complexity of the treatment and the quality of the materials used. Since each patient has different needs, prices are determined individually and may vary depending on the details of the treatment. Therefore, the most appropriate treatment plan and pricing for each patient should be determined by the dentist.

Dental and oral health covers much more than just dental health. Gums, the tissue that protects teeth, nerves and nerves, have an extremely sensitive structure. Like teeth, gums also need regular care. If regular care is not performed, the possibility of serious health problems in the gums and the risk of developing chronic diseases should not be ignored. Gum itching is one of these periodontal diseases.

There can be many reasons for itchy gums, from allergic reactions to various dental health problems. Gums are the soft tissue that surrounds the teeth and provides a seal around each tooth. Healthy gums are very important for protecting teeth. Itching is often a sign that there is bacteria between the teeth and gums.

Itchy gums are usually easy to treat, and maintaining good dental hygiene can prevent most problems. In some cases, itching can be a sign of more serious conditions such as gum disease. Therefore, if symptoms persist, a dentist should be consulted.
What Causes Itchy Gums?
Itchy gums are a symptom that can occur for various reasons. The main causes of itchy gums are as follows:

Periodontal disease: Periodontal diseases such as gingivitis and periodontitis are one of the most common causes of itchy gums. These diseases cause inflammation of the gums due to plaque buildup. This inflammation can cause your gums to become red, swollen, and itchy.

Brushing and flossing: Itchy gums can also be caused by improper brushing and flossing techniques. Applying too much pressure to your gums or using a toothbrush that is too hard can cause your gums to become irritated. Remember that deep cleaning does not mean applying pressure to the teeth. Good quality and soft toothbrushes are effective in brushing teeth in preventing itchy gums.
Dentures or other oral appliances: If you wear dentures or other oral appliances, such as braces, they may come into contact with your gums and cause irritation.
Hormonal changes: Hormonal changes such as pregnancy, menopause, and menstruation can cause gums to become sensitive and itchy.
Medications: Some medications can have side effects that can cause itchy gums. Especially antidepressants, antihistamines and blood thinners can cause this condition.
Tartar: Tartar that builds up on your teeth can irritate your gums and cause itching.
Allergies: Some foods and drinks taken orally can cause allergic reactions in the gums, causing itching.
Systemic diseases: People with systemic diseases such as diabetes or immune system may experience itchy gums.

Itchy gums can be an important sign that you need to pay attention to your gum health and overall oral health. If your gum itching persists or is severe, you should consult a dentist or dental specialist. Treatment allows us to identify the underlying cause and apply appropriate treatment.
How to Prevent Gum Itching
Follow these steps to prevent and treat itchy gums:
It is important to brush and floss at least twice a day to keep your gums healthy and prevent gum itching. It is important to learn proper brushing and flossing techniques.

Dental Exams: Regular dental exams are important to check the health of your gums and get professional cleanings if necessary. We are happy to welcome you to the Dentaliva Dental clinic, usually twice a year.
Healthy eating habits: A balanced diet supports healthy gums. Consuming foods containing vitamins A, C, E and minerals can have a positive effect on your gums.
Smoking and Alcohol: Smoking and excessive alcohol can negatively affect your gum health. It is important to avoid or reduce these habits.
Itchy Gum Treatment

Treatment of periodontal disease: If gum itching is a symptom of periodontal disease, our dentists will recommend a treatment plan. Mild cases, such as gingivitis, may be easier to treat, while more serious cases, such as periodontitis, may be more extensive to treat. The goal of these treatments is to improve the health of your gums.
Medications: Medications such as antibiotics and mouthwash may be prescribed for gum diseases and other gum problems.
Adjust your dentures: If your dentures or appliances are putting pressure on your gums or causing irritation, you may need to adjust or readjust them.
Treatment of hormonal changes: If hormonal changes cause itching in the gums, treatment options may include hormone therapy or adjustments to hormonal changes.
Allergy Management: It may be helpful to limit exposure to allergens or use allergy medications to protect itchy gums from allergic reactions.

Itchy gums can be a sign of serious periodontal disease, so you should always contact your dentist if your symptoms persist or become severe. Our professional exams and expert doctors can help you improve your gum health.
Methods Used in the Treatment of Gum Itching

To effectively treat itchy gums, it is necessary to pinpoint the cause. If the itching is caused by periodontal disease, our dentists will usually recommend gum treatment or teeth cleaning. In mild cases, more regular and effective dental hygiene may be sufficient. If itchy gums indicate more severe gum disease, more extensive treatment may be needed. This may include professional intervention to control gingivitis and improve gum health. Gum itching can be caused by hormonal changes, allergies, dentures, etc. If it occurs due to various reasons, we use different treatment methods. If itching is caused by hormones, hormonal therapy or appropriate lifestyle changes may be recommended. If the itching is caused by an allergy, you may need to avoid the allergen or use allergy medication. Itchy gums should be examined and treated by a professional dentist, as proper treatment is important in making gums strong and comfortable.
What Happens If Gum Itching is Left Untreated?

If itchy gums are left untreated, it can cause a variety of adverse effects that can lead to serious oral health problems. This condition often occurs as a symptom of periodontal disease and may progress further. If periodontal disease is left untreated, the gums become inflamed, bleed frequently and recede. This can lead to exposure of the tooth root and eventual tooth loss. Additionally, the discomfort, pain and swelling caused by gum itching can become chronic and negatively affect daily life. Gum disease not only affects your oral health, but can also cause systemic health problems. If you experience itching gums or symptoms of periodontal disease, contact us for early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Dental and oral health covers much more than just dental health. Gums, the tissue that protects teeth, nerves and nerves, have an extremely sensitive structure. Gum itching is one of these periodontal diseases.

There can be many reasons for itchy gums, from allergic reactions to various dental health problems. Gums are the soft tissue that surrounds the teeth and provides a seal around each tooth. Healthy gums are very important for protecting teeth. Itching is often a sign that there is bacteria between the teeth and gums.

## What Causes Itchy Gums?
Itchy gums are a symptom that can occur for various reasons. The main causes of itchy gums are as follows:

Periodontal disease: Periodontal diseases such as gingivitis and periodontitis are one of the most common causes of itchy gums. These diseases cause inflammation of the gums due to plaque buildup. This inflammation can cause your gums to become red, swollen, and itchy.

Brushing and flossing: Itchy gums can also be caused by improper brushing and flossing techniques. Applying too much pressure to your gums or using a toothbrush that is too hard can cause your gums to become irritated. Remember that deep cleaning does not mean applying pressure to the teeth. Good quality and soft toothbrushes are effective in brushing teeth in preventing itchy gums.
Dentures or other oral appliances: If you wear dentures or other oral appliances, such as braces, they may come into contact with your gums and cause irritation.
Hormonal changes: Hormonal changes such as pregnancy, menopause, and menstruation can cause gums to become sensitive and itchy.
Medications: Some medications can have side effects that can cause itchy gums. Especially antidepressants, antihistamines and blood thinners can cause this condition.

Dental veneer is a medical dental aesthetic procedure performed on the front surface of the tooth, which eliminates discolorations, caries and possible deformities on the surface of the tooth. There are various types of dental veneers, depending on the veneer material used during the procedure. When choosing these materials, factors such as the structure of the tooth, the age of the person who will have it done, and any disorders occurring in the tooth are taken into consideration.

Metal-based porcelain dental veneer, empress dental veneer, composite dental veneer, porcelain veneer and zirconium dental veneer are the most common dental veneer types in beautiful smile aesthetics. The type of dental veneer to be applied during treatment is selected according to the needs and demands of the patient.
Metal-Based Porcelain Dental Veneer

The metal infrastructure that forms the lower part of the metal-supported porcelain veneer is usually made of titanium or gold alloy. This metal infrastructure increases the durability of the tooth and ensures the durability of the prosthesis. At the same time, this infrastructure helps the dentist shape and personalize the prosthesis.

A thin porcelain coating is applied over the metal infrastructure. Porcelain provides an aesthetic appearance and color similar to natural teeth. Additionally, porcelain allows teeth to reflect light naturally, providing a natural appearance. However, due to the underlying metal layer, this type of veneer is not as advantageous as the new veneer types in terms of light.
Empress Dental Veneer

Empress veneers are porcelain composite veneer types whose durability rate is further increased by strengthening the ceramic piece by placing glass ceramics on it. No metal is used in this type of dental coating. The content consists of ceramics.

This type of veneer is known for transmitting light quite well. It is also highly preferred in prosthetic procedures. In other words, it is frequently used in aesthetic applications. Thus, we can say that it is used in lamination processes.

Successful results are also achieved in patients who have problems with their front teeth. It can also be applied to molars, where the force is less emphasized compared to the front teeth. Successful results are achieved with empress veneers for these teeth. Age-related discolorations, root canal treated teeth, and people with gapped teeth are other dental treatments in which empress veneers are used.

The light transmittance of Empress coatings is quite good and color controls can be made. In this way, a beautiful natural look is achieved. This natural appearance provides the person with a beautiful aesthetic smile.
Porcelain Laminate Veneers

Porcelain laminate veneers look very natural because they are made to match the shape and color of your natural teeth, so it is difficult to predict which tooth is a veneer and which is not. Porcelain composite veneers are strong, long-lasting and resistant to staining.

There is no reversal in this process, because a small section of the tooth enamel must be removed in order for the veneer to be placed on the tooth. Therefore, it is necessary to be sure to have these dental procedures done before having veneers.
Porcelain laminate veneers are made in the dental laboratory. The first step is to schedule a preliminary consultation with your dentist to determine the improvements you want.

We create a mock-up (rehearsal teeth design) to show you a preview of your new and improved smile. After you accept the treatment plan, we prepare your teeth by removing a small amount of tooth enamel from the front and sides of the teeth to be crowned. Next, we take impressions of your teeth and send them to the dental laboratory. We also determine the tooth color before the impressions are sent to the dental laboratory.

Your dentist may attach temporary teeth to your teeth because it usually takes 1-2 weeks for the crown to be applied in the dental laboratory. When the veneers arrive from the laboratory, you and your dentist confirm whether the shape, fit and color of the tooth are good. Your dentist will bond the prepared veneers onto your teeth with a light-sensitive resin. The material hardens under a special light, which bonds the veneer securely to the tooth enamel. The final touch is leveling and polishing the composite resin to give it a natural appearance.

Composite resin is a cheaper material that is tooth-colored and is often used for laminate veneers. Composite veneers can be made in a dental laboratory with the same process steps as porcelain laminate veneers.
Zirconium Dental Veneers

Zirconium is an element that has ceramic properties but is in the metal group in the periodic table. It does not have the flexibility feature like metals, but has a strength comparable to metals in terms of bite resistance. In metal-supported porcelain crowns, fractures may occur over time when the porcelain separates from the metal due to chewing forces. However, developed monolithic zirconium crowns are one piece and do not cause such surface fractures called “chipping” when no porcelain layer is added on them.

Zirconium tooth restoration is a type of coating applied mostly to eliminate severe caries, tooth fractures and discoloration of teeth. Yttrium tetragonal stabilized zirconia crystal is used for use as a dental ceramic. Although its fragility continues, its transparency feature has been improved, especially with the new generation monolithic forms produced in recent years. Thus, it has the feature of imitating the naturalness of the teeth that are tried to be created similar to them.
Zirconium dental veneers are not used for the treatment of decayed teeth. However, zirconium veneers compatible with the gum and cut tooth can prevent further tooth decay.

There are no additives in zirconium dental veneers. It is considered stronger, harder and more resistant to fractures when compared to glass ceramics and dental composites. Thanks to this structure, it has a structure that can prevent cracking, breaking and chipping in the teeth underneath.

Veneers are a permanent solution, so make sure you are fully informed about your treatment options before deciding which material is better for you. With the help of your dentist, you can determine whether you are a suitable patient for veneers and find the best way to improve your smile. You can ask us any questions about dental veneer types. Our customer representatives and specialist dentists will be happy to answer your questions and assist you.
